title_ko: The Role of Translation-Assisted ChatGPT Engagement in Enhancing Grammar Proficiency: Insights from TOEIC Performance
title_en: The Role of Translation-Assisted ChatGPT Engagement in Enhancing Grammar Proficiency:Insights from TOEIC Performance
kw_ko: ChatGPT(챗GPT); Grammar Learning(문법학습); TOEIC (토익); Artificial Intelligence(인공지능); Language Education(언어교육); Translation Experience (번역경험)
abstract_ko: This study investigates the potential of ChatGPT-assisted learning for improving English grammar proficiency among undergraduate students. Over a semester-long course, students engaged in translation tasks, grammar explanations, and sentence correction activities using ChatGPT, and their engagement patterns were compared to standardized TOEIC-based grammar test outcomes. The analysis examined relationships among ChatGPT utilization, translation experience, future intention to use AI tools, and grammar performance. Results showed that higher levels of ChatGPT utilization were moderately to strongly associated with improved grammar scores (r = .55), with each one-point increase in utilization predicting an estimated 8.3-point gain in TOEIC grammar performance (R² = .31). Translation experience also demonstrated a positive association, while future intention to use ChatGPT exhibited only a weak relationship with actual achievement. These findings highlight the pedagogical value of structured, active engagement with AI tools and underscore the need for instructional designs that balance AI support with learner autonomy to prevent over-reliance and promote sustained language development.

title_ko: 생성형 AI 시대의 영작문 과제 수행 패턴 변화: 사이버대학 대학생들을 대상으로
title_en: Changes in English Writing Assignment Performance Patterns in the Era of Generative AI: A Study of Online University Students
kw_ko: 생성형 AI; 온라인 영작문 교육; 사이버대학; 과제 수행 패턴; 시계열 분석
kw_en: Generative AI; Online English Writing Education; Online University; Assignment Performance Patterns; Time-Series Analysis
abstract_ko: 2022년 11월 ChatGPT 출시 이후 온라인 교육에서 학생들의 과제 수행 방식에 대한 우려가 제기되었다. 본 연구는 2022년 1학기부터 2024년 2학기까지 6개 학기 동안 국내 한 사이버대학교에서 수집된 영작문 과제 데이터를 분석하여 시간에 따른 과제 수행 패턴의 변화를 탐색하였다. 623명 학생이 제출한 44,697개 문장을 분석 대상으로 하였으며, 학생들을 기말시험 성적에 따라 세 그룹으로 분류하고 2022년과 2023-2024년 두 시기로 구분하여 주어진 단어 사용률, 문장 길이, 고유 단어 수, Type-Token Ratio의 변화를 분석하였다. 연구 결과, 모든 성취도 그룹에서 통계적으로 유의한 변화가 관찰되었으며, 고유 단어 수는 16% 이상 증가하였고 문장 길이는 18% 증가한 반면 주어진 단어 사용률은 약 3% 감소하였다. 주어진 단어 사용률은 2022년 2학기와 2023년 1학기 사이에서만 큰 변화를 보였으나, 다른 지표들의 변화 시점은 다양하게 나타났다. 그룹별 변화 크기는 유사하였으며, 예상과 달리 하위 그룹이 가장 큰 변화를 보이지 않았다. 본 연구는 사이버대학 학생들의 영작문 패턴에 의미 있는 변화가 있었음을 확인하였으나, 이를 단일 요인으로 설명하기는 어렵다는 점을 시사한다.
abstract_en: The release of ChatGPT in November 2022 raised concerns about how students perform assignments in online education. This study explored temporal changes in English writing assignment patterns by analyzing data collected over six semesters from Spring 2022 to Fall 2024 at a Korean online university. The analysis examined 44,697 sentences submitted by 623 students classified into three groups based on final exam scores. The study compared two periods (2022 vs. 2023-2024) across four writing characteristics: given word usage rate, sentence length, unique word count, and Type-Token Ratio. Results showed statistically significant changes across all achievement groups, with unique word count increasing by over 16%, sentence length by 18%, and given word usage rate decreasing by approximately 3%. Given word usage rate showed its largest change only between Fall 2022 and Spring 2023, while other indicators changed at various time points. The magnitude of change was similar across groups, with the Low group not showing the largest change as initially expected. This study confirms meaningful changes in online university students’ writing assignment patterns during 2022-2024, while suggesting these changes cannot be attributed to a single factor.

title_ko: A Case Study on Using ChatGPT for English Writing and Speaking Classes: Focused on Seventh Grade Students
title_en: A Case Study on Using ChatGPT for English Writing and Speaking Classes: Focused on Seventh Grade Students
kw_en: ChatGPT/English as a foreign language/writing/speaking/perception
abstract_ko: This case study investigates the integration of ChatGPT in seventh-grade English writing and speaking instruction over a four-week period with 130 Korean EFL students. Data were collected through comprehensive questionnaires, semi-structured interviews, and systematic classroom observations to assess implementation effectiveness. Quantitative analysis using a five-point Likert scale revealed strong attitudinal benefits, with students rating class participation highest, followed by content understanding and learning interest. Language skill perceptions, particularly speaking abilities, showed more moderate improvement. Qualitative findings demonstrated ChatGPT’s dual functionality: first, as a comprehensible input provider delivering personalized, level-appropriate responses aligned with Krashen’s Input Hypothesis (1985); second, as an interaction catalyst facilitating peer negotiation of meaning consistent with Long’s Interaction Hypothesis (1981). Students reported significantly reduced anxiety in ChatGPT-mediated activities compared to traditional instruction, attributing increased participation to the absence of peer judgment and evaluation pressure. Collaborative activities positioned ChatGPT as a shared resource generating authentic peer-to-peer communication opportunities. Results indicate ChatGPT’s immediate impact centers on affective factors and peer interaction facilitation rather than direct skill development outcomes. This study provides empirical evidence for AI integration in EFL contexts, demonstrating how generative AI effectively addresses authentic communication challenges while supporting the 2022 revised English curriculum’s emphasis on integrated, competency-based learning.

title_ko: Learner Use of AI Feedback in English Writing: Effects of AI Feedback in Writing according to Learner Traits
title_en: Learner Use of AI Feedback in English Writing: Effects of AI Feedback in Writing according to Learner Traits
kw_en: AI feedback/self-efficacy/wiring proficiency/trust in AI feedback
abstract_ko: This study investigates how learners engage with AI feedback in English writing tasks and examines how learners’ initial writing proficiency, self-efficacy, and trust in AI feedback influence both writing performance and feedback usage behavior. The research involved approximately 40 university students with prior experience using AI-based feedback tools. Participants completed a diagnostic writing test, two questionnaires measuring writing self-efficacy and trust in AI feedback, four essay-writing tasks, and a post-writing test. Quantitative data were analyzed using SPSS 28.0 to examine relationships among learner variables and writing outcomes. The findings indicate that AI feedback alone does not guarantee improvement; rather, learners’ perceptions of feedback, motivational factors, and contextual guidance provided by instructors play a critical role in effective feedback uptake. In addition, the results suggest that structured instructional support can enhance learners’ ability to interpret and apply AI-generated feedback meaningfully. Based on these findings, the study offers practical implications for AI feedback system design, including the incorporation of emotionally sensitive language, contextual personalization, and educator-facilitated feedback interpretation. Future research should further investigate longitudinal effects and a wider range of text genres and learner populations to strengthen the pedagogical validity of AI-assisted feedback.

title_ko: PBL 기반 영어교사교육에서 AI 보조교사 활용과 교사 주도성 발현
title_en: The use of AI Co-teachers and the manifestation of teacher agency in PBL-based English teacher education
kw_ko: 인공지능/보조교사/교사주도성/문제해결중심학습법
kw_en: artificial intelligence/co-teacher/teacher agency/problem-based learning
abstract_ko: This study examined how pre-service English teachers in a Problem-Based Learning (PBL) context perceived and utilized AI as a co-teacher and how their teacher agency emerged throughout the process. Seventeen third-year pre-service English teachers from C University’s English education department participated in this study. The method involved participants engaging in a team-based PBL project using AI tools of their choice, and their reflective journals and lesson plans were analyzed qualitatively through thematic analysis. Findings showed that participants viewed AI not as a mere technological tool but as a collaborative partner and reflective resource that enhanced their pedagogical thinking. During lesson design, they demonstrated professional judgment by critically interpreting and adapting AI-generated suggestions to align with pedagogical goals and students’ needs. Their understanding of the teacher’s role evolved into that of a human-centered mediator who balances AI–learner interactions, emphasizing emotional feedback, ethical reasoning, and empathy as essential human capacities that AI cannot replicate. In conclusion, AI functioned not as a replacement but as a collaborative tool that supported the development of teacher professionalism and agency. The PBL-based instructional experience effectively supported pre-service teachers in strengthening human-centered educational values and developing a responsible attitude toward AI integration in English education.

title_ko: 자연어처리 원리 중심 인공지능 융합 영어 읽기 수업 설계원리 개발
title_en: Development of instructional design principles for AI-integrated English reading classes, focusing on NLP
kw_ko: 자연어처리; 인공지능 리터러시; 인공지능 융합 수업; 영어 읽기 수업; 수업 설계원리
kw_en: natural language processing (NLP); AI literacy; AI-integrated classes; English reading instruction; instructional design principles
abstract_ko: 최근 인공지능 리터러시 함양을 위한 수업으로 인공지능 융합 수업이 주목받고 있다. 인공지능의 하위 영역 중 자연어처리는 인간의 언어 능력을 모방하고자 발전해 온 기술로 영어 교과와 밀접한 관련이 있으며, 영어 학습과 인공지능 리터러시를 함양할 수 있는 잠재력을 지닌다. 본 연구는 자연어처리원리를 중심으로 인공지능 융합 영어 수업을 설계할 수 있는 수업 설계원리와 상세지침을 개발하고그 타당성을 검증하고자 하였다. 이를 위해 선행문헌 검토 및 전문가 면담을 통해 설계원리를 도출하고 전문가 검토를 통해 설계원리를 수정하였다. 중학교 3학년 학습자 20명을 대상으로 설계원리를 적용하고 인공지능 리터러시, 영어 학습 흥미도에 대한 사전․사후 검사, 설문조사, 면담을 실시하여 외적 타당화를 거쳤다. 그 결과 6개의 설계원리와 21개의 상세지침을 도출하였으며, 이를 적용한 수업은인공지능 리터러시 및 영어 읽기 태도 향상에 대한 긍정적 효과를 보였다. 본 연구는 인공지능 기술을 영어 교과의 학습 목표를 달성하기 위해 활용하는 것에 그치지 않고, 인공지능의 개념 및 원리에대한 깊이 있는 이해와 영어 학습 내용 간의 융합을 시도했다는 점에서 의의가 있으며, 영어 교과에서 자연어처리를 주제로 한 인공지능 융합 수업의 가능성에 대한 시사점을 제공한다. 한편, 본 연구는단일 학급을 대상으로 효과성을 확인하였으며, 자연어처리 기술 중 워드 임베딩 개념을 중심으로 수업이 진행되었다는 점에서 일반화에 한계가 있다. 향후 연구에서는 자연어처리의 다양한 하위 개념및 기술이 포함된 수업 내용과 대규모 학습자 대상의 검증을 통해 외적 타당성이 보완될 필요가 있다.
abstract_en: Recently, AI-integrated classes have gained attention as an approach to fostering AI literacy. Natural language processing (NLP) has developed through efforts to emulate human language abilities and thus shares strong relevance with English education, holding potential to promote both English learning and AI literacy. This study aims to develop and validate instructional design principles for designing AI-integrated English classes centered on NLP principles. To this end, instructional design principles were derived through a review of previous literature and expert interviews, and subsequently refined through expert validation. The principles were applied to 20 third-year middle school students, and external validation was conducted through pre- and post-tests, surveys, and interviews examining AI literacy and interest in English learning. As a result, six instructional design principles and twenty-one detailed guidelines were developed, and the applied lessons demonstrated positive effects on AI literacy and attitudes toward English reading. This study attempts not merely to use AI technologies to achieve English curriculum goals, but to integrate an in-depth understanding of AI concepts and principles with English learning content, offering implications for the potential of NLP-based AI-integrated English instruction. However, this study examined effectiveness within a single class and focused mainly on word embeddings among various NLP concepts, indicating limitations in generalizability. Future research should incorporate broader NLP components and conduct large-scale evaluations to strengthen external validity.
note: NLP 원리 융합 영어 읽기 수업 설계원리 개발·타당화

title_ko: AI 시대 비서직 영어역량 탐색: 고경력 비서들의 경험을 중심으로
title_en: Exploring English Competence for Secretarial Work in the AI Era: A Study of Experienced Professionals
kw_ko: 비서 영어역량; 인공지능(AI); 생성형 AI; 특수목적영어(ESP) 교육; 디지털 업무 환경
kw_en: Secretarial English Competence; English for Specific Purposes (ESP); Digital Work Environment; Artificial Intelligence (AI); Generative AI
abstract_ko: 인공지능(AI: Artificial Intelligence)의 비약적 발전에 따라 비서가 갖춰야 할 영어역량이 변화하고 있지만, 아직까지 업무 현장에서 비서들이 경험하는 영어업무의 변화상을 조사한 연구를 찾아볼 수 없다. 본 연구는 AI 시대의 비서가 갖춰야 할 영어능력과 이에 상응하는 교육을 탐색하고자, 첫째, 비서직 영어업무에 AI는 어떻게 활용되고 있는가? 둘째, AI 시대에 필요한 직무 영어능력은 무엇인가? 셋째, AI 시대에 비서직 영어교육에 고려할 내용은 무엇인가? 라는 연구 문제를 수립하였다. 연구 문제를 해결하기 위해 경력 10년 이상의 5명의 현직 비서들의 면담 자료를 수집, 분석하는 정성적 연구 방법을 사용했다. 도출된 연구 결과는 다음과 같다: 첫째, 비서 영어업무를 수행 과정에서 AI는 원어민 에디터이자 업무의 조력자로 활용되고 있다. 둘째, 비서가 AI를 활용하여 자신이 수행한 영어업무에 대한 확신을 가지려면 높은 수준의 독해력과 실시간 구두소통 능력이 뒷받침되어야 한다. 셋째, 비서직 영어교육에 AI를 적극적으로 활용하는 효과적인 특수목적영어(ESP) 교육이 고려되어야 한다. 도출된 결과를 토대로 인공지능 시대 비서가 지녀야 할 핵심적인 영어능력은 첫째, 돌발 상황이 빈번히 일어나는 업무 현장에서 즉시 의사소통할 수 있는 능력, 둘째, 문화적인 뉘앙스까지 파악할 수 있는 통합적 독해능력이라는 결론에 도달할 수 있었다. 본 연구의 결론은 비서 영어교육에 있어서, AI 도구를 적극적으로 활용하는 교육이 추가적으로 필요하며, ESP 관점에서의 전문분야 독해 및 말하기 교육이 더욱 확장될 필요가 있다는 점을 시사한다. 본 연구는 생성형 AI, ChatGPT가 상용화된 2022년 이후 비서의 영어업무 경험을 실증적으로 조사하여 분석한 최초의 연구라는 점에서 의의가 있다.
abstract_en: Although the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has brought significant changes to the English competence required of secretaries, little research has examined how secretaries experience these changes in actual workplace settings. To address this gap, this study aimed to explore the English competencies required of secretaries in the AI era and the corresponding implications for English education by posing the following research questions: (1) How is AI utilized in English-related secretarial work? (2) What job-related English competencies are required in the AI era? (3) What aspects should be considered in English education for secretarial professionals in this context? To answer these questions, a qualitative research method was employed, involving the collection and analysis of interview data from five practicing secretaries with over ten years of professional experience. The findings are as follows. First, in the process of performing English-related tasks, AI is utilized as a native-level editor and as a supportive assistant. Second, secretaries’ confidence in AI-assisted English work is underpinned by a high level of reading comprehension and the ability to engage in real-time oral communication. Third, effective English for Specific Purposes (ESP) education that actively incorporates AI tools should be considered for secretarial English training. Based on these findings, the study concludes that the core English competencies required of secretaries in the AI era include, first, the ability to communicate immediately in workplace situations where unexpected issues frequently arise, and second, an integrated reading competence that enables the interpretation of cultural nuances. These conclusions suggest that English education for secretarial professionals should further incorporate instruction that promotes the active use of AI tools and expand ESP-based reading and speaking education tailored to professional domains. This study is significant in that it represents the first empirical investigation into secretaries’ English work experiences since the commercialization of generative AI, such as ChatGPT, in 2022.
note: 비서 직무 영어에서 AI 활용 면담, ESP 교육 시사점 도출

title_ko: 생성형 인공지능을 활용한 영어 교육 연구 동향 분석: 체계적 문헌 고찰과 텍스트 마이닝을 중심으로
title_en: Trends in English language education using generative artificial intelligence: A study focusing on systematic review and text mining
kw_ko: 생성형 인공지능; 컴퓨터 보조 언어학습; 영어 교육; 언어 학습
kw_en: ChatGPT; generative AI; Computer-Assisted Language Learning (CALL); English education; language; learning
abstract_ko: 본 연구는 ChatGPT가 공개된 이후 시점인 2023년 1월부터 2025년 8월의 기간에 걸쳐 출판된 생성형인공지능(Generative AI)을 활용한 제2언어 학습 활동을 다룬 연구 166편을 대상으로 체계적 문헌 고찰, 키워드 분석, 그리고 잠재 디리클레 할당(LDA) 토픽모델링을 실시하였다. 분석 결과, 연구 참여자 학교급에 있어서 84.9%에 달하는 연구가 고등교육 맥락에서 이루어졌다. 연구 방법에 있어서는 양적 연구와 혼합 연구가 절대 다수를 차지했으며(91.0%), 질적 연구의 비율은 단 9%에 그쳤다. 연구 참여자규모는 50명 이상 100명 미만의 연구가 가장 많은 비율을 차지했으며(42.2%), 학습 도구는 ChatGPT와같은 기성 생성형 AI 모델을 직접 활용한 비율이 가장 높았다(73.5%). 연구 수행 맥락 및 언어 기능학습 결과는 쓰기 영역이 66.3%로 가장 많았으며, 감정, 몰입, 동기와 같은 정의적 학습 결과와 메타인지, 창의성과 같은 기타 학습 결과도 다루어졌다. 주제 분포의 불균형으로 인해 쓰기 영역과 비(非) 쓰기 영역을 분리하여 각각 토픽 모델링을 실시하였다. 쓰기 영역 분석 결과, (1) 생성형 AI 쓰기 피드백 구조와 특성, (2) 생성형 AI 쓰기 피드백 효과 및 학습 성과, (3) 생성형 AI 통합 쓰기 수업 설계, (4) 쓰기 파트너로서의 생성형 AI와 인간 협력의 네 가지 토픽이 산출되었다. 비(非)쓰기 영역 분석 결과, (1) 생성형 AI 활용 오류 교정과 학습 확장, (2) 생성형 AI 기반 챗봇 상호작용과 학습 동기․참여, (3) 생성형 AI 기반 학습에서의 고차적 사고와 수행, (4) 생성형 AI 기반 의미 중심 언어 학습과 정서변화의 네 가지 토픽이 산출되었다. 분석 결과를 바탕으로 본 연구는 학습자, 교수자, AI의 역할에 대한 재고와 언어 교육의 특수성을 반영한 생성형 AI 기반 영어 학습 설계의 필요성을 논의한다.
abstract_en: This study conducted a systematic literature review integrating keyword analysis and Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) topic modeling of 166 studies on second language (L2) learning involving generative artificial intelligence (Gen AI). Results showed that 84.9% of the studies were situated in higher education. Quantitative and mixed-methods designs dominated (91.0%), while qualitative studies accounted for only 9%. Most involved 50-100 participants (42.2%), and off-the-shelf Gen AI models comprised 73.5% of learning tools used. Writing was the most frequently studied (66.3%), and affective and other learning outcomes were also explored. Due to the uneven distribution of topics, the writing and non-writing domains were separated and topic modeling was conducted independently for each. Analysis of studies in the writing domain yielded four topics: (1) AI Writing Feedback Structure and Characteristics, (2) Effects of AI Writing Feedback and Learning Outcomes, (3) Designing Writing Instruction Integrated with AI, and (4) AI-Human Collaboration as Writing Partners. Analysis of studies outside the writing domain produced another set of four topics: (1) AI-Assisted Error Correction and Learning Expansion, (2) Motivation and Engagement through AI Chatbot Interaction, (3) AI-Mediated Higher-Order Thinking and Performance, and (4) Affective Changes in Meaning-Focused Language Learning with AI. The study discusses the evolving roles of learners, teachers, and AI and the need for learning design that reflects the specific characteristics of language education in the era of Gen AI.
note: 생성형AI 영어교육 연구 166편 체계적 고찰·토픽모델링

title_ko: 메타버스 환경에서의 생성형 AI 기반 일본어 상호문화 교수･학습 프로그램 개발 및 타당성 검증
title_en: Development and Validation of a Generative AI–Based Japanese Intercultural Teaching and Learning Program in a Metaverse Environment
kw_ko: 생성형 AI; 상호문화 역량(ICC); 메타버스; 일본어교육
kw_en: Generative Artificial Intelligence; Intercultural Communicative Competence (ICC); Metaverse; Japanese Language Education
abstract_ko: 본 연구는 메타버스(Metaverse)와 생성형 인공지능(Generative AI)을 융합한 일본어 상호문화 교수·학습 프로그램을 설계하고, 그 교육적 타당성을 검증하는 것을 목적으로 하였다. Byram(1997)의 상호문화역량(ICC) 모형을 기반으로 한 6차시 프로그램을 대학 일본어 학습자 29명을 대상으로 실시하였다. 양적 분석 결과, 학습자의 ICC가 모든 하위 영역에서 유의미하게 향상되었으며, 질적 분석을 통해 몰입적 상호작용, 문화적 성찰, 표현 전략의 확장, 자기주도적 학습 강화 등의 변화를 확인하였다. 본 연구는 AI와 메타버스의 결합이 일본어교육을 언어 중심에서 문화 공존 중심으로 확장하는 가능성을 보여준다.
abstract_en: This study aimed to design and validate a Japanese intercultural teaching–learning program integrating the Metaverse and Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI). Based on Byram's (1997) Intercultural Communicative Competence (ICC) model, a six –session program was implemented with 29 university learners of Japanese. Quantitative results showed significant improvements across all ICC subdomains, while qualitative findings revealed enhanced immersive interaction, cultural reflection, pragmatic expression strategies, and learner autonomy. The integration of AI and Metaverse technologies demonstrated the potential to transform Japanese language education from a linguistic focus toward a culturally coexistent paradigm.
note: 일본어 상호문화 프로그램

title_ko: 일본 고전문학 수업의 생성형AI 활용
title_en: A Study on the Integration of Generative AI in Japanese Literature Education
kw_ko: 일본 문학 교육; 고전문학; 생성형AI; 디지털인문
kw_en: Japanese Literature Education; Classical Japanese Literature; Generative AI; Digital Humanities; TBL
abstract_ko: 본 논문은 대학의 일본문학 수업, 특히 고전문학 교육에서 나타나는 학습자의 흥미 저하와 텍스트 이해의 어려움을 극복하기 위한 디지털 기술 활용 방안을 모색한 결과 보고이다. 플립러닝, 디지털 매핑, 메타버스 등의 기술을 도입한 교수법의 다변화는 새로운 기술 도입으로 학생들의 흥미 유발에는 성공했지만, 설명 위주 강의가 가지는 근본적인 한계를 해소하기에는 부족함이 있었다. 이에 본 논문에서는 고전문학을 다루는 <일본문학개론> 수업에 생성형 AI를 적극 도입한 사례를 소개하고 그 의의와 한계를 분석했다. 수강생들은 수엊에서 생성형AI를 사용해 문학작품의 개요, 문학용어, 사회적 배경에 대해 조사하며 교수자의 강의만으로는 알기 어려운 사항을 보완할 수 있었다. 나아가 교수자는 생성형AI의 답변을 활용한 질문을 작성하는 과제를 제출하여 수강자의 지식의 확장을 꾀했다. 결과적으로 생성형AI는 초개인맞춤형 교육도구로서 충분히 기능했다고 할 수 있다.
abstract_en: This study explores the application of digital technology to overcome persistent challenges in university Japanese literature courses, particularly in classical literature education. These challenges include low student engagement and difficulties in textual comprehension. While previous courses attempted to diversify teaching methods by introducing technologies such as flipped learning, digital mapping, and the metaverse, these efforts were insufficient to overcome the fundamental limitations of traditional lecture–centric instruction. Accordingly, this paper proposes a new educational model that actively integrates generative AI, with the goal of applying it to the <Introduction to Japanese Literature> course in 2025. The specific implementation strategies are as follows: First, utilizing AI image generation tools to visualize key scenes from classical works, such as *The Tale of Genji*, thereby concretizing the abstract nature of the texts. Second, employing AI to translate and summarize difficult classical texts into modern language, which enhances learners' reading accessibility. Third, co–creating scenarios and drafts for oral presentations with generative AI. These attempts suggest new possibilities for the future direction of Japanese classical literature education in the digital age.
note: 일본 고전문학 수업

title_ko: 다차원적 메타버스 플랫폼 기반 영어 발표 수업: 학습자 변인과 학습성과
title_en: Multi-Dimensional Metaverse Platform-Based English Presentation: Learner Factors and Learning Outcomes
kw_en: metaverse-based learning; blended learning; English presentation; learner characteristics; metaverse literacy
abstract_ko: This study explored how to design and apply a blended learning model for English presentation classes using two metaverse platforms, ZEP and CoSpaces. The research examined how students’ prior interest in the metaverse and their digital skills affected their learning outcomes. Twenty-seven university students took part in a 15-week blended course. ZEP was used for real-time interaction and group work, while CoSpaces supported 3D content creation and virtual presentations. Data were gathered through online surveys before and after the course, including both quantitative items and open-ended questions. Descriptive and correlational analyses were conducted with SPSS 20.0, and qualitative responses were analyzed using thematic analysis. Overall learning experiences were highly positive (M = 3.94, SD = 0.96), with course interest (M = 4.22, SD = 0.85) and learning comprehension via blended learning (M = 4.22, SD = 0.76) also highly positive. Prior interest in the metaverse among learners was positively correlated with aspects of interest in the course (r = .53, p < .05), motivation to learn (r = .41, p < .05), and presentation confidence (r = .39, p < .05). Digital device proficiency was highly positively correlated with all aspects of metaverse literacy, including proficiency with ZEP functionality (r = .61, p < .01), design ability in CoSpaces (r = .47, p < .05), and virtual presentation (r = .58, p < .01). Qualitative findings indicated three main positive outcomes: decreased anxiety and enhanced confidence (44.1%), innovative learning experiences (29.4%), and increased engagement and enjoyment (20.6%). Overall, the results suggest that prior metaverse interest relates more to affective outcomes related to interest, motivation, and confidence, while digital device proficiency has a stronger connection to cognitive outcomes of metaverse literacy. At the same time, there remains an opportunity to develop differentiated instructional support that accounts for individual differences among learners. Furthermore, it recommends pre-course orientation and mentoring to address digital disparities and ensure effective blended learning design.

title_ko: Analyzing Linguistic Gains and Interaction Patterns in ChatGPT-Assisted L2 Writing Revision: A Case Study of Adult EFL Learners
title_en: Analyzing Linguistic Gains and Interaction Patterns in ChatGPT-Assisted L2 Writing Revision: A Case Study of Adult EFL Learners
kw_en: ChatGPT; learner-ChatGPT interaction; prompt engineering; linguistic features; ChatGPT usage purposes
abstract_ko: This study investigates how adult EFL learners interact with ChatGPT during writing revision and examines how these interactions affect the linguistic features of their revised texts. Using a case study approach, the research collected self-introductory essays written before and after revision from four adult EFL learners, along with reflection logs detailing their purposes for using ChatGPT and the prompts they used. Linguistic features were analyzed using text analysis tools within the Complexity, Accuracy, and Fluency framework. The Wilcoxon signed-rank test assessed differences, and matched-pairs rank biserial correlation measured effect sizes. Thematic analysis was applied to explore participants’ purposes and prompt usage patterns. Five major findings emerged: (1) learners mainly used ChatGPT for lexical and syntactic corrections, rarely for content, style, or structural development; (2) prompts were generally simple, lacking contextual depth; (3) the use of vague autocomplete prompts suggested a personified view of ChatGPT; (4) multi-turn interactions were limited, even when the responses were unsatisfactory; and (5) while ChatGPT supported micro-level improvements in grammar, lexical variety, and readability, its impact on content elaboration and the overall length of the text was minimal. These findings highlight both the instructional potential and the constraints of using ChatGPT as a revision aid in second language writing.

title_ko: Engagement with Language through ChatGPT Use: A Systematic Review
title_en: Engagement with Language through ChatGPT Use: A Systematic Review
kw_en: ChatGPT; EWL; language learning; affordances; engagement with language
abstract_ko: This study aims to understand how the use of ChatGPT for English language learning affects learners’ attention to language as measured through engagement with language (EWL). EWL is significant as it is attention to language and is understood to be the application of explicit language knowledge and the process that updates this knowledge. To accomplish this, a systematic review and qualitative analysis of research exploring ChatGPT and its effects on EWL were conducted. Recent empirical studies were selected, and the reported data were coded to identify evidence of EWL states and processes across its three subdimensions of affective, cognitive, and social EWL. The findings show that ChatGPT use does offer affordances for EWL. ChatGPT encouraged affective EWL as it provides motivation, reduced anxiety, and a sustained willingness to engage with language. Cognitive EWL was elicited through heightened attention to linguistic form, reflective problem-solving, and critical appraisal of AI-generated feedback. Social EWL was facilitated as learners initiate and maintain dialogic interactions with the model, negotiate meaning, and exercise agency in shaping the direction of exchanges. The study concludes with pedagogical implications and recommendations for future research.

title_ko: 미적 경험의 교육적 변주 - AI․디지털 융합 현대시 공간 교육
title_en: Educational Variations on Aesthetic Experience - AI and Digital Convergence: Poetry Space Education
kw_ko: 현대시 교육; AI․디지털 융합 문학교육; 메릴; 교수설계; 현대시 공간 교육
kw_en: Modern poetry education; AI and digital convergence literature education; Merrill; instructional design; modern poetry space education
abstract_ko: 본 연구는 AI․디지털 융합 현대시 공간 교육을 통해 미적 경험을 확장하는 교육 모형을 Merrill의 핵심교수설계 원리(First Principles of Instruction)를 기반 으로, 설계하고자 한다. 특히 지역성과 시의 공간성을 결합하여 학습자가 현대 시 속 공간을 시각적․체험적으로 재구성하고, 이를 통해 시적 감수성과 창의성 을 동시에 신장시키는 것을 목표로 하였다. 연구에서는 ‘문제 인식–활성화–시 연–적용–통합’의 단계에 AI․디지털 도구를 적극적으로 통합하여, 학습자의 자기주도적 창작과 비판적 해석을 촉진하였다. 연구 결과, 제안된 모형은 전통 적 해석 중심 수업의 한계를 극복하고, STEAM․Maker 교육 등 융합형 문학교육과 연계 가능성이 높음을 확인하였다. 본 연구는 AI․디지털 융합 시대 현대 시 교육의 새로운 방향을 제시하며, 향후 다양한 지역문학 교육 및 창의융합 수업 설계의 확장 가능성을 시사한다.
abstract_en: This study aims to design an educational model that expands aesthetic experience through AI- and digital-integrated contemporary poetry spatial education, based on Merrill’s First Principles of Instruction. Specifically, the study aims to combine regionality and the spatiality of poetry, enabling learners to visually and experientially reconstruct the spaces within contemporary poetry, thereby simultaneously fostering poetic sensibility and creativity. The study actively integrated AI and digital tools into the stages of “problem recognition-activation-demonstration-application-integration” to promote learners’ self- directed creation and critical interpretation. The results confirmed that the proposed model overcomes the limitations of traditional interpretation-centered classes and has high potential for integration with integrated literature education such as STEAM and maker education. This study suggests a new direction for modern poetry education in the era of AI and digital convergence, and suggests the potential for expanding the design of diverse regional literature education and creative convergence classes in the future.

title_ko: 바이브코딩을 통한ACME 플랫폼 개발: 영어교육과 학생을 위한 인공지능 기반 진로‧학습‧상담 지원모델 연구
title_en: Integrating Vibe Coding into ACME: An AI-Driven Career, Learning, and Counseling Platform for English Education Majors
kw_en: ACME; AI-based career support platform; vibe coding; English education majors
abstract_ko: This study develops ACME, a comprehensive AI-based career support platform built through vibe coding. The ACME platform integrates four interconnected modules: Assistant AI, which supports preparation for the Secondary School English Teacher Recruitment Exams using a dataset of 806 English test items from 2002–2025 along with 365 documented success narratives systematically collected from Naver blogs (n = 167), online teacher certification communities (n = 101), university recruitment archives (n = 34), and YouTube interviews/vlogs (n = 63); Consultant AI, facilitating non-teaching career exploration through employment database integration and labor market intelligence; Mediator AI, coordinating institutional resources with individual career planning; and Educator AI, providing teaching methodology support via curated educational technology tools. Drawing on three primary data sources: (1) institutional records of career and extracurricular program participation (2022–2024), (2) a pre-survey of 54 English education majors, and (3) a post-pilot usability test involving 36 students—the study examined English education majors’ career identities, advising needs, and platform effectiveness. Findings from a preliminary needs assessment (n = 54) revealed significant career development challenges: while students demonstrated strong major satisfaction (55.6%) and interest (61.1%), only 44.4% expressed confidence in their career readiness confidence. Career aspirations fluctuated dramatically across academic years (first/second year: 76.9%/70.0%; third year: 33.3%; fourth year: 66.7%), reflecting students’ evolving awareness of teaching market realities. Demand for career counseling services tripled between 2022-2024 (20 to 61 annual participants), yet specialized programming for non-teaching careers markedly declined. A pilot evaluation (n = 36) confirmed platform utility, with highest ratings for examination preparation (M = 4.44) and teaching methodology resources (M = 4.36). Qualitative analysis revealed student requests for enhanced functionality including automated error-pattern detection, expanded non-teaching career outcome databases, community-based peer matching, and career-aligned activity recommendations. The study validates vibe coding as an effective method for enabling sustainable, low-cost platform development, demonstrating that regional universities can autonomously create department-level, discipline-specific AI systems supporting personalized, data-driven career guidance.

title_ko: 영어 AI 디지털교과서에 대한 고등학생의 인식: 영어학습 성취도에 따른 비교
title_en: High School Students' Perceptions of English AI Digital Textbooks: A Comparison Based on English Learning Achievement
kw_en: AI digital textbook; English learning; perception; achievement level; self-directed learning; emotional stability
abstract_ko: As artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly transforms education, the AI Digital Textbook (AIDT) has emerged as a key innovation for personalized and interactive learning. This study examined high school students’ perceptions of using the English AIDT according to their English achievement levels. A total of 149 first-year high school students who had used the AIDT in English classes participated in the study. Data were collected through surveys and open-ended responses from students, as well as in-depth interviews with both students and teachers. The survey measured four categories (i.e., self-directed learning, level-based learning, functional aspects, and emotional stability). The findings showed that students generally held positive perceptions of the AIDT, particularly regarding its functional convenience and feedback system. However, self-directed learning received the lowest mean score, revealing that autonomy and self-regulated learning strategies have not yet been fully developed within the AIDT environment. The statistical results indicated that students showed significantly different perceptions across the four categories with self-directed learning scoring significantly lower than the other three categories. When comparing the two groups by achievement level, higher-achieving students generally showed more positive perceptions. However, significant differences were found only in emotional stability, suggesting that immediate feedback may enhance motivation for higher achievers but cause anxiety for lower achievers. Overall, while the AIDT supports personalized and interactive learning, its effective use also depends on instructional guidance that fosters learner autonomy and provides emotional support for students at different achievement levels.

title_ko: AI기반 영어 읽기 문항 자동 출제 방안 탐색
title_en: Exploring AI-Based Automatic Item Generation for English Reading Comprehension
kw_en: Automatic Item Generation; generative language model; open-source model; closed-source model; education assessment
abstract_ko: This study aimed to explore the theoretical foundations of automatic item generation (AIG) methods and derive practical implications by examining the quality of English reading items automatically produced using generative language models, in order to support item writers seeking efficient development of high-quality items. To this end, open-source (Llama) and closed-source (ChatGPT) models were selected and test items were generated under four sets of conditions to compare the outcomes. These conditions specified eight variables — standard performance, item type, genre, topic, keyword, number of options, language and text length — to ensure maximal consistency between the two language models. Based on these conditions, two item types were pilot-generated for 7th- and 10th-grade students: identifying specific details and identifying mood/emotion changes. Subsequently, ten content experts evaluated the quality of the generated items. The results indicated that although test items produced by generative language models still require improvement and are not yet ready for immediate use in school settings, there was no meaningful difference in quality between the items generated by the open-source and closed-source models. These results suggest that institutions sensitive to data security may consider developing automatic generation systems based on open-source models.

kw_ko: 생성형 인공지능(GAI) 활용 교육; 인공지능 리터러시 교육; 교수학습 프레임워크; 비판적 읽기; 쓰기 윤리; 신뢰성 검증; 프롬프트 생성 전략; 학습자 주도성
kw_en: Education using Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI); AI literacy education; teaching and learning frameworks; critical reading; writing ethics; reliability verification; prompt generation strategies; student agency
abstract_ko: 본고의 목적은 생성형 인공지능(GAI) 활용 교수학습 프레임워크에 기반한 국어과 수업 사례에서 학습자의 생성형 인공지능 활용 양상을 분석하여 인공지능 리터러시(AI literacy) 교육적이며 국어교육적인 시사점을 도출하는 데 있다. 연구 방법은 문헌 연구, 델파이 조사, 수업 실행 및 분석이다. 주요 연구 내용으로는 먼저 교과 융합 교육 및 범교과 교육에 적용될 수 있는 GAI 활용 교수학습 프레임워크(KERIS의 GATe 프레임워크)의 개발 과정, 델파이 조사를 통한 타당화 과정에서 부각된 국어과 수업 실행 설계의 쟁점 및 해소 방향을 논의하였다. 이어서 국어과 수업 실행 사례에서 학습자의 GAI 활용 양상을 귀납적으로 분석한 결과, 신뢰성 검증, 프롬프트 작성 및 조정에 문제가 있음을 발견하였다. 이를 근거로 사실 확인 및 중복 점검 등의 확장된 비판적 읽기와 쓰기 윤리, 프롬프트 생성 전략 등의 인공지능 리터러시 교육적이자 국어 교육적 지도가 필요한 내용을 논의하였다. 특히 2023년과 2025년이라는 약 2년의 시차가 있는 사례를 통해, GAI의 대중화 초기와 확산기의 측면, 출처 표시 기능 등 GAI의 기능 진화에 따른 변화 측면에서 학습자들의 활용 양상을 해석하고 교육적 대처 방안을 제시하였다.
abstract_en: This study aims to explore the application of a generative artificial intelligence (GAI)-based teaching and learning framework (the KERIS GATe Framework) to Korean language education and to identify key issues and solutions through a Delphi survey and classroom analysis. An inductive analysis of learners’ GAI utilization in Korean language classrooms revealed the need for expanded critical reading and writing ethics grounded in student agency, such as fact-checking and reliability verification, as well as prompt generation strategies, offering implications for both AI literacy and Korean language education. Specifically, the study examines how changes in ChatGPT’s functionalities from 2023 to 2025 have impacted learners’ utilization patterns and suggests educational strategies to address these changes.

title_ko: ChatGPT의 평가와 피드백에 나타난 프레이밍 효과: 탐색적 혼합 연구
title_en: Framing Effects on ChatGPT’s Evaluation and Feedback: An Exploratory Mixed-Methods Study
kw_en: ChatGPT; framing effect; AI feedback; assessment reliability; framing literacy
abstract_ko: This study examined how ChatGPT’s evaluation and feedback patterns varied when identical text was framed as ‘student text’ or ‘AI revision.’ An exploratory mixed-methods design was employed, in which 66 argumentative essays written by university students were assessed under two framing conditions, and ChatGPT’s rubric-based scores and feedback were collected for comparison. The quantitative analysis indicated that ChatGPT assigned higher scores when an essay was presented as an ‘AI revision’ rather than as a ‘student text,’ with the largest differences observed in grammar and language use. The qualitative analysis further revealed distinct differences in tone, evaluative orientation, feedback function, and meta-evaluation. Under the ‘AI revision’ framing, ChatGPT provided more encouraging and reinforcement-oriented feedback, whereas under the ‘student text’ framing, the feedback was more critical and evaluative. These findings suggest that ChatGPT’s responses are influenced not only by textual features but also by contextual framing information, with its role shifting from an evaluator under the ‘student text’ framing to a facilitator under the ‘AI revision’ framing. Pedagogically, the study highlights the need for framing literacy, encouraging teachers and learners to recognize the contextual dependence and potential biases of AI feedback and to engage with it more critically.

title_ko: AI 영어회화 앱 의인화 유형에 따른 사용자 경험 차이 분석
title_en: Analyzing User Experience Differences by Anthropomorphism Type in AI English Conversation Apps
kw_ko: AI 의인화 유형; 사용자 경험; 몰입도; 심리적 부담; 학습 만족도; 영어 회화 숙련도
kw_en: AI Anthropomorphism Types; User Experience; Immersion; Psychological Burden; Learning Satisfaction; English Conversation Proficiency
abstract_ko: 오늘날 AI 기술의 발전은 영어 교육 환경의 변화를 이끌고 있으며, 특히 AI 의인화 유형 영어 회화 애플리케이션은 학습자에 게 몰입도 높은 개인화된 학습 경험을 제공하고 있다. 본 연구는 대화형 AI 의인화 유형이 사용자 경험(몰입도, 심리적 부담, 학습 만족도)에 미치는 영향을 분석하고, 영어 회화 숙련도에 따른 차이를 탐색하고자 하였다. 이를 위해 국내외 AI 영어 회 화 애플리케이션 8종을 분석하여 음성/텍스트 기반, 동물 캐릭터 기반, 사람 캐릭터 기반, 사람 실물 기반의 네 가지 AI 의인 화 유형을 도출하였다. 이후 성인 학습자 100명을 숙련도 상·하 집단으로 구분한 뒤 동일 과제를 기반으로 각 인터페이스를 체험하게 하고, 설문조사와 심층 인터뷰를 통해 정량·정성 데이터를 수집하였다. 분석 결과, 사람 실물 기반 인터페이스는 전체적으로 가장 높은 몰입도와 학습 만족도를 보였으나 초급 학습자에게는 심리적 부담을 유발하는 경향이 있었다. 반면 동물 캐릭터 및 음성/텍스트 기반 인터페이스는 초급 학습자의 몰입 유지와 부담 완화에 효과적이었다. 이러한 결과는 영어 회화 숙련도에 따라 AI 의인화 유형의 효과가 달라짐을 보여준다. 본 연구는 학습자 영어 회화 숙련도 수준에 따라 적합한 인터페이스 유형을 달리 적용할 필요성을 시사하며, 향후 개인화된 UX 설계 및 영어 교육 플랫폼 전략 수립에 기초 자료를 제공할 수 있을 것으로 기대된다.
abstract_en: The advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) technology is reshaping the landscape of English education, with AI-based anthropomorphic conversation applications offering learners highly immersive and personalized learning experiences. This study examines the impact of conversational AI anthropomorphism types on user experience (Immersion, psychological burden, and learning satisfaction) and explores differences according to learners’ proficiency in English conversation. To this end, eight AI conversation applications were analyzed to identify four anthropomorphism types: text/voice-based, animal character- based, human character-based, and human-like interfaces. One hundred adult learners were then divided into high- and low-proficiency groups and asked to perform identical tasks with each interface. Quantitative and qualitative data were collected through surveys and in-depth interviews. The analysis revealed that human-like interfaces produced the highest overall Immersion and learning satisfaction but tended to increase psychological burden for lower-proficiency learners. In contrast, animal character-based and text/ voice-based interfaces were more effective in maintaining Immersion and reducing burden among lower- proficiency learners. These findings demonstrate that the effects of AI anthropomorphism vary depending on learners’ proficiency levels. The study highlights the necessity of tailoring interface types to learner proficiency and is expected to provide practical insights for the design of personalized user experience (UX) and the development of AI-based English education platforms.
note: AI 영어회화 앱 의인화 유형별 사용자 경험 설문·면담

title_ko: University Students’ Meaning-Making and Participation in an AI-Supported Collaborative English Course
title_en: University Students’ Meaning-Making and Participation in an AI-Supported Collaborative English Course
kw_en: AI-supported learning; collaborative inquiry; language construction; learner participation; prompt literacy
abstract_ko: This study explores university students’ learning experiences in a collaborative, inquiry-based general English course that employed a range of AI-supported tools. Throughout the course, students used AI-supported generative systems, such as ChatGPT, to produce and refine texts, while non-generative AI-supported tools, like Papago and Natural Readers, supported translation, summarization, and text-to-speech tasks. Together, these AI-supported resources shaped how learners constructed meaning, processed information, and participated in collaborative activities. When fifty student artifacts, including group reports, reflective journals, and open-ended survey responses, were analyzed qualitatively four main themes emerged: (1) expanded and multilayered language-construction processes, (2) evolving structures of collaborative participation, (3) progressive development of AI-supported prompt-formulation strategies, and (4) affective responses tied to the use of AI-supported tools. Students described comparing AI-generated drafts, negotiating meaning with peers, and refining their ideas as they moved between tools. Many learners also noted that practicing prompts repeatedly helped them better control the quality of their output and use AI-supported tools more strategically. For several students, AI-supported assistance reduced anxiety, particularly in speaking and presentation tasks. Overall, the findings suggest that AI-supported tools collectively influence how learners construct meaning, collaborate with peers, and manage emotional aspects of learning. These insights offer important implications for designing AI-supported English instruction and understanding the teacher's evolving role in technology-mediated classrooms.

title_ko: 영어학습자 글쓰기의 수준 유지형 GPT 기반 텍스트 증강과 디코딩 온도 조건의 효과 —실증 연구
title_en: Level-Preserving GPT-Based Text Augmentation for EFL Learner Writing: Effects of Decoding Temperature
kw_en: ChatGPT-based text augmentation; level-preserving augmentation; decoding temperature; EFL learner writing; hybrid score
abstract_ko: This study examines whether ChatGPT-based text augmentation can preserve learner writing levels and how decoding temperature influences augmentation quality and stability. We augmented 141 English texts written by Korean EFL university students (CEFR B1–B2) under five temperature settings (0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9), producing 695 candidate texts. Augmentation quality was assessed using a composite hybrid score integrating level preservation, lexical diversity, and structural stability. For each source text, the highest-scoring candidate was selected, yielding 139 original–augmented text pairs for subsequent analyses. Results show that the augmented texts achieved partial level preservation: they largely maintained relative proficiency ordering and macro-level text scale (e.g., word and sentence counts), while permitting limited shifts in local lexical and syntactic features. Across conditions, temperature 0.5 showed the highest selection frequency and the lowest variability, indicating the most consistent balance between expressive diversity and structural stability for level-preserving augmentation.

title_ko: Speaking English with AI or Humans: What Engages EFL Learners More?
title_en: Speaking English with AI or Humans: What Engages EFL Learners More?
kw_en: AI; peer interactions; speaking performance; EFL university students
abstract_ko: This study investigated the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) and peer interactions on the speaking performance and attitudes of EFL university students using a within-subjects design. Thirty-nine participants engaged in both AI-based and peer-based speaking activities over 14 weeks and completed pre- and post-speaking tests, as well as pre-, mid-, and post-questionnaires. At the end of the semester, they also submitted reflective essays describing their experiences. Results revealed significant improvements in both speaking performance and self-perceived speaking skills from pre- to post-test. However, students’ attitudes toward AI and peer interactions diverged. Engagement, interest, and participation in AI interactions declined over time, whereas these affective dimensions in peer interactions remained stable or improved. Enjoyment and concentration were also consistently higher in peer interactions than in AI interactions. Overall, the findings suggest that although AI can enhance EFL learners’ speaking performance through repetitive practice and timely feedback, peer interactions play a more enduring role in supporting engagement, enjoyment, and meaningful language learning over time.

title_ko: 학교 영어 말하기 교육을 위한 맞춤형 AI 말하기 진단-학습-평가 시스템 설계 연구
title_en: A study on the design of a customized AI-based speaking diagnosis, learning, and assessment system for public English education
kw_ko: AI 기반 학습 진단 시스템; 자동 말하기 채점; 말하기 평가
kw_en: AI-based diagnosis system; automated speaking scoring (ASS); speaking assessment
abstract_ko: The purpose of this study is to develop and implement a customized AI-based speaking diagnosis, learning, and assessment system, SpeakMaster, in order to overcome the lack of systematic evaluation and practice opportunities in school English speaking class. This system integrates automated speaking scoring to provide students with feedback on their speaking abilities across pronunciation, conversation, and presentation. This study adopts a design-based research methodology, demonstrating the development and implementation process. 1,451 students and eight teachers in elementary, middle, and high schools participated in the experiment. Data were collected through learning logs, teacher journals, interviews, and post-surveys. The findings indicate that the system design is appropriate for English class, promoting students’ flow in engaging speaking practice. Students showed motivation and satisfaction while teachers found the system valuable for monitoring student progress and facilitating speaking assessments. Despite the challenges of improving chatbot performance and enhancing scoring reliability, the results suggest that SpeakMaster shows potential to enhance English speaking education.

title_ko: ChatGPT in Enhancing Speaking Skills in Language Learning: A Systematic Review
title_en: ChatGPT in Enhancing Speaking Skills in Language Learning: A Systematic Review
kw_en: ChatGPT; Generative AI; AI in Education; Language Learning; Speaking Skills; Systematic Review; PRISMA
abstract_ko: The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in education has created new opportunities to enhance learners’ oral communication skills. Yet, previous systematic reviews have primarily focused on writing and assessment, leaving a gap in understanding how large language models (LLMs), particularly ChatGPT, support speaking development. This systematic review analyzed 19 peer-reviewed empirical studies published between 2023 and 2025, retrieved from ERIC, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and Web of Science. Eligible studies examined ChatGPT-assisted speaking instruction or practice across varied educational settings and learner populations. Findings indicated that ChatGPT-supported activities such as dialogues, role-plays, and debates enhanced learners’ fluency, vocabulary use, pronunciation, and communicative confidence. Integrating AI as a scaffolded conversational partner also increased motivation and self-regulation, especially when embedded within teacher-guided pedagogical frameworks. This review extended prior research by offering the first comprehensive synthesis of ChatGPT’s role in speaking skill development and by identifying both pedagogical benefits and persistent challenges related to prompt design, extended interaction, and ethical considerations. The results provided concrete recommendations for educators and policymakers seeking to integrate generative AI responsibly into language learning, emphasizing the need for structured implementation, teacher mediation, and ongoing evaluation to ensure sustainable and equitable educational outcomes.

title_ko: Associations between ChatGPT Use and Perceived Educational Outcomes among Chinese International Students in South Korea: A Mixed-Methods Study
title_en: Associations between ChatGPT Use and Perceived Educational Outcomes among Chinese International Students in South Korea: A Mixed-Methods Study
kw_en: ChatGPT; Higher Education; Application; Positive Associations; Negative Associations
abstract_ko: This study examines how Chinese international students in South Korea use ChatGPT. We analyze both the benefits they perceive and the risks they may encounter. The research employs a mixed-methods design that combines surveys and interviews. We surveyed 200 Chinese graduate students at Universities A and B in South Korea. We also conducted semi-structured interviews with 15 of these students. The inquiry focuses on several key areas: how often and in what situations students use ChatGPT, their learning goals, self-reported outcomes, and their concerns about academic integrity. Participants reported several positive effects. These include a perceived improvement in their academic performance and receiving personalized learning support. ChatGPT also helped stimulate deeper thinking by allowing rapid exploration of ideas. Additionally, it aided in accessing and organizing educational resources and in language-related tasks such as reading, drafting, and revising texts in a foreign language. However, students also reported several risks. These potential problems include violating academic integrity, such as using AI assistance without proper disclosure. Other concerns are that ChatGPT might weaken independent learning habits, reduce opportunities for critical reflection, and sometimes provide inaccurate or misleading information. Based on these findings, the paper offers recommendations. Universities should create clear guidelines for using ChatGPT. They should also design assessments that promote original student work. Furthermore, instructors should provide training on crafting effective prompts, verifying information from AI, and citing its use properly. We encourage institutions to acknowledge the educational value of tools like ChatGPT. At the same time, they must maintain safeguards and support systems to ensure students use this technology responsibly. The overall goal is to help Chinese students at Korean universities use ChatGPT more effectively and appropriately in their learning processes.

title_ko: 영어 쓰기에서 AI 피드백 학습활동이 대학생의 영어 성취도와 쓰기 동기에 미치는 영향
title_en: The effects of AI feedback learning activities in English writing on university students’ English achievement and writing motivation
kw_ko: AI 피드백 학습활동; 영어 성취도; 영어 쓰기 동기; 대학생
kw_en: AI feedback learning activity; English achievement; English writing motivation; university students
abstract_ko: This study investigates how AI feedback learning activities in English writing classes affect university students’ English achievement and writing motivation. It examines both cognitive and affective outcomes in EFL contexts using generative AI tools such as ChatGPT. A total of 244 first-year university students completed four writing tasks incorporating AI feedback during the revision process. Pre- and post-tests were conducted along with the Oxford Placement Test (Syndicate, 2001) and a modified version of Payne’s (2012) Academic Writing Motivation Questionnaire. Quantitative analyses revealed significant improvement in English achievement and three motivational subcomponents—enjoyment, recognition, and effort—while instrumentality showed no significant change. Qualitative analysis of open-ended questionnaire responses indicated that students valued AI feedback for error detection, coherence, and self-directed learning, yet recognized limitations such as unnatural expressions, misinterpretations, and overreliance on AI. The findings highlight the importance of AI literacy and propose a hybrid feedback model integrating AI and teacher guidance to enhance learner autonomy and writing competence.

title_ko: 생성형 AI 를 활용한 맞춤형 영어 읽기 자료 생성: 중등 교육과정 기반 GPT 모델 개발을 기반으로
title_en: Curriculum-based GPT model development and evaluation for customized English reading material creation
kw_ko: 생성형 인공지능; 교육과정 기반 텍스트 생성; Coh-Metrix 분석; 수준별 수업
kw_en: generative AI; curriculum-based text generation; Coh-Metrix analysis; differentiated instruction
abstract_ko: This study aims to develop and evaluate a GPT-based English learning system that creates reading materials tailored to the Korean middle school first-grade English curriculum. To this end, this study adopted OpenAI’s MyGPTs platform and created the AI system through eight different developmental versions by iterating prompts and uploading relevant knowledge files. To evaluate its linguistic appropriateness, this study generated reading passages at three difficulty levels (low, medium, high) and compared them with eight textbook texts using seventeen key indices from Coh-Metrix 3. The results show that GPT-generated texts at the medium level most closely resembled actual textbook passages in sentence count, syntactic simplicity, lexical familiarity, and overall readability. Low-level outputs achieved the highest readability and concreteness scores, indicating suitability for beginner EFL learners, while high-level outputs featured greater syntactic complexity, longer sentences, and richer lexical diversity. The study also identified limitations in GPT’s consistent adherence to prescribed difficulty parameters, text-type variety, and adaptive difficulty adjustment based on learner performance.

title_ko: 진로교과 통합교육 기반 생성형 AI 영어듣기 콘텐츠 개발 및 적용: 사범대 영어교육과 사례를 중심으로
title_en: Development and application of AI-generated English listening content through career and subject integration: Focusing on English education majors
kw_ko: 진로교과 통합교육; 생성형 인공지능; 영어듣기교육
kw_en: career-subject integrated education; generative AI; English listening education
abstract_ko: This study presents a career-integrated English education model incorporating generative AI through two tracks: (1) content development, where English education majors in four career-oriented groups (teaching vs. non-teaching; decided vs. undecided) created TOEIC-format listening materials aligned with their interests; and (2) classroom application, where the AI-generated content was implemented in first-year general classes with 103 students. Career maturity was measured by a 30-item scale, and content effectiveness by ratings of difficulty, appropriateness, usefulness, and effectiveness. Results showed that content-related factors, not learner background, best predicted overall satisfaction. Although no statistically significant differences were found, education majors tended to rate the materials as slightly more useful and slightly less difficult. Pre–post tests showed improved decisiveness, suggesting that AI-integrated, career-oriented instruction enhanced students’ confidence in career decision-making and demonstrated the potential of generative AI in fostering professional competence and career readiness.

title_ko: A Meta-analysis of ChatGPT’s Effects on English Writing in Korean Classrooms
title_en: A Meta-analysis of ChatGPT’s Effects on English Writing in Korean Classrooms
kw_en: ChatGPT; L2 writing instruction; feedback in writing; meta-analysis; research synthesis
abstract_ko: This meta-analysis synthesizes evidence on the effects of ChatGPT-assisted instruction on English writing in Korean EFL contexts. A systematic search in RISS yielded 401 records; after screening under PRISMA procedures, 12 studies reporting writing outcomes were included and analyzed. Effect sizes were computed as Hedges’ g and pooled using random-effects models. The random-effects mean indicated a medium-to-large improvement in writing (g = 0.6867). Mixed-effects subgroup analyses detected no statistically significant differences by experimental design (pre-experimental vs. quasi-experimental), educational level (tertiary vs. secondary), or region (metropolitan vs. others). Meta-regression trends for duration (weeks, positive) and weekly intensity (sessions/week, negative) were suggestive but not statistically significant. Overall, ChatGPT-supported writing instruction yields meaningful gains and shows consistent effects at both secondary and tertiary levels; in practice, it is well suited to complement teacher feedback. Future studies should expand samples in secondary and non-metropolitan settings and employ stronger designs to clarify how duration and intensity shape outcomes.

title_ko: English Education Majors’ Practices and Perceptions of AI Use: Opportunities and Ethical Challenges
title_en: English Education Majors’ Practices and Perceptions of AI Use: Opportunities and Ethical Challenges
kw_en: Artificial Intelligence (AI); pre-service English teachers; Technology Acceptance Model (TAM); academic integrity; English education
abstract_ko: This study examined pre-service English teachers’ perceptions, applications, and ethical orientations toward AI tools in English education. A mixed-methods survey was administered to 59undergraduates, combining a 40-item quantitative scale with open-ended responses, and analyzed using descriptive statistics, group comparisons, and thematic analysis. Findings revealed three major patterns. First, participants perceived AI as useful for reducing burden, enhancing efficiency, and supporting lesson preparation, but their actual applications remained limited to basic functions, highlighting a perception–practice gap. Second, usage frequency in the data showed clear threshold effects: moderate use supported efficiency gains, while only high-frequency engagement enabled recognition of creative or higher-order benefits. Duration of use, by contrast, had weaker and less consistent effects, underscoring that intensity of engagement matters more than exposure length. Third, concerns about overreliance, creativity decline, fairness, plagiarism, and reliability were stable across groups, reflecting baseline normative orientations. Interpreted through the Technology Acceptance Model (Davis, 1989), students’ emphasis on efficiency and burden reduction aligned with perceived usefulness. However, reliability concerns fall outside core Technology Acceptance Model (TAM)constructs, pointing to the need for complementary theoretical perspectives. Beyond TAM, the findings highlight ethical and normative dimensions as essential to AI adoption in teacher education. The study underscores the dual task of fostering meaningful engagement with AI while safeguarding integrity—an issue of particular urgency in Korea, where AI-driven digital textbooks will be introduced nationwide in 2025.

title_en: Elementary School Teachers' Perceptions on the Use of English AIDT
kw_ko: AI 디지털교과서; 초등교사; 인식 연구; 초등영어교육; 교사 교육
kw_en: AIDT; elementary school teachers; perception study; English education in elementary schools; teacher education
abstract_ko: The study aims to examine the perceptions of elementary school teachers regarding the use of English AIDT. A questionnaire consisting of ten open-ended questions was used with ten elementary school teachers who had experience using English AIDT in classes or through teacher training programs. The results showed that most participants expressed positive views on the change in legal status of AIDT from textbooks to educational materials. It was also found that as positive aspects of using English AIDT, participants mentioned the customized learning tailored to students' levels and the individual feedback function, and as negative aspects, they pointed out the increased burden on teachers and the reduced opportunities of interactions with teachers and peers. Lastly, participants proposed teacher training programs on the use of AIDT and digital literacy education for students for the efficient use of English AIDT.

title_ko: AI–인간 평가자 간 독해 지문 난이도 평정 비교: 9급 국가직 공무원 영어시험 (2019~2023년)을 중심으로
title_en: A Comparison of AI and Human Raters in Reading Text Difficulty Ratings: Focusing on the Grade 9 National Civil Service English Examination (2019~2023)
kw_ko: 9급 공무원 영어시험; 지문 난이도; AI CEFR 기반 분석; 인간 평가자 분석; AI-인간 지문 난이도 평정 비교
kw_en: Grade 9 National Civil Service English; Text Difficulty; AI-Based CEFR Analysis; Human Rater Analysis; Comparison of AI and Human Text Difficulty
abstract_ko: This study examined the degree of agreement between AI-based CEFR difficulty analyses and human raters’ judgments of English reading passages from the Korean Grade 9 National Civil Service Examination (2019–2023). Fifty passages were analyzed using the Cathoven AI CEFR Checker, and six trained human raters independently evaluated text difficulty on a five-point scale. Weighted Cohen’s κ and Spearman’s ρ were used to examine inter-rater reliability and AI–human agreement. Results showed moderate to high agreement among human raters but relatively low alignment between AI and human ratings. AI tended to overestimate difficulty in texts with complex syntax and advanced vocabulary, whereas human raters emphasized content familiarity and cognitive accessibility, suggesting that AI can serve as a complementary assessment tool providing objective linguistic indicators rather than replacing human judgment.

title_ko: Unlocking the Impact of AI-Assisted Online Interactive Learning Environment in English Language Learning
title_en: Unlocking the Impact of AI-Assisted Online Interactive Learning Environment in English Language Learning
authors: Ranta Butarbutar(Universitas Musamus Merauke, Indonesia); Sujarwo(Universitas Megarezky, Indonesia); Ermelinda Agnes Gunu Pure(Universitas Musamus Merauke, Indonesia); Sulviana(Universitas Islam Makassar, South of Sulawesi, Indonesia); Abdul Rizal(Universitas Musamus Merauke, Indonesia)
kw_en: Artificial Intelligence; ELSA speak; English language learning; Google Docs; online interactive learning
abstract_ko: This study investigates the impact of Online Interactive Learning Environments (OILE) integrated with AI technologies on students' English Language Learning (ELL) skills, specifically focusing on reading, writing, speaking, and listening. The research involved 50 English major students, divided into control and intervention groups, and utilized AI-assisted tools such as WhatsApp Groups, Google Documents, ELSA Speak, and Zoom to enhance interactive and personalized learning experiences. The results demonstrated significant improvements across all assessed areas, indicating the effectiveness of these interventions. The data revealed notable enhancements in reading comprehension, writing development, speaking proficiency, listening comprehension, vocabulary acquisition, and pronunciation accuracy. This study highlights the potential of AI-assisted OILE to create engaging, interactive, and personalized learning environments that foster active student participation and improve overall language proficiency. These findings contribute to the ongoing global discourse on the role of artificial intelligence in education, offering practical implications for educators, curriculum designers, and policymakers who aim to transform traditional EFL classrooms into dynamic interactive learning spaces. Future research should focus on optimizing these technologies to address specific skill deficits and to enhance the efficacy of AI-assisted language learning.

title_ko: Navigating Support: EFL Students’ Questions and Decisions Between ChatGPT and Teachers in L2 Writing
title_en: Navigating Support: EFL Students’ Questions and Decisions Between ChatGPT and Teachers in L2 Writing
authors: Judy Yin(Korea National University of Education)
kw_en: ChatGPT; EFL writing; student questioning; prompt literacy; feedback collaboration
abstract_ko: This study investigates how EFL undergraduates distribute their writing-related questions between ChatGPT and their instructor by highlighting the distinct yet complementary roles of each. Seventeen first-year students majoring in English education in Korea participated in a 15-week composition course where they produced drafts, asked questions to both sources, and reflected through journals and interviews. Analysis of these data revealed that students consulted ChatGPT primarily for translation support, vocabulary alternatives, sentence flow, and idea generation, while directing questions about nuance, cultural appropriateness, depth, and evaluation to their instructor. Decisions were shaped not only by convenience and access but also by metacognitive awareness of ChatGPT’s limitations and concerns about authorship. Students described using AI as a resource for exploration while ultimately relying on the instructor as the authoritative guide for academic expectations and readability. These findings underscore questioning as a central feedback-seeking practice and suggest that writing instruction can benefit from positioning ChatGPT and teacher feedback as complementary, rather than competing, supports.

title_ko: 우리나라 대학생들의 ChatGPT 및 동료와 영어 말하기 비교 분석
title_en: A Comparative Analysis of ChatGPT- and Peer-Based English Speaking Practice of Korean College Students
kw_ko: AI기반 영 어 말하기; 동료 기반 영어 말하기; 챗지피티; 대화 분석; EFL 학습자
kw_en: AI-based English speaking; peer-based English speaking; ChatGPT; conversation analysis; EFL learners
abstract_ko: The purpose of this study was to analyze and compare the characteristics of Korean college students’ conversations with ChatGPT and peers in the classro om, in terms of turn-taking, adjacency pairs, repair sequence, and sequence organization of their conversations. A total of 20 conversations from ChatGPT- and peer-based English speaking practice were analyzed through the Conversation Analysis (CA) procedure qualitatively (Heritage, 1984; Sacks et al., 1974). Also, Python 3.14 (2025) was employed to analyze the number of turn-taking, adjacent pairs, repair sequence, and sequence organization, quantitatively. Results of data analysis indicated that the students exchanged more turns in conversations between peers than in those with ChatGPT. Adjacent pairs of conversations were also found to have used a larger number of adjacent pairs in peer-based conversations. The students repaired 3.8 times in the conversation with ChatGPT while repairing 13.4 times with their peers. In the part of sequence organization, there is no significant difference between conversations with ChatGPT and peers. Based on the results of data analysis, pedagogical implications and suggestions for effectively utilizing AI devices in the Korean EFL classroom are presented.

title_en: Exploring the Impacts of EduTech-Integrated English Lesson Design Practicum on University Students’ Digital Literacy, EduTech-Use Efficacy, and Attitude
kw_ko: 디지털 문해력; AI 통합 영어 수업; 에듀테크 활용 효능감; 수업 설계 실습; 학습자 태도
kw_en: digital literacy; AI-integrated English instruction; EduTech-use efficacy; lesson design practicum; learner attitude
abstract_ko: This study explored the impacts of an EduTech-integrated lesson design practicum on university students majoring in English, focusing on three key aspects: digital literacy, EduTech-use efficacy, and attitude. Twenty-one students participated in a 15-week course that integrated various EduTech tools－Copilot, Nearpot, Goosechase, and Padlet－into collaborative, process-based tasks. The study drew on two primary sources of data: surveys and group interviews conducted with a cohort of 12 participants The quantitative results from the Wilcoxon signed-rank test revealed statistically significant improvements across all three dependent variables. Thematic analysis of the interview data further uncovered multidimensional growth in awareness, including digital ethics, metacognitive knowledge, self-belief in EduTech utilization, and reflective practices－elements not fully captured by the survey data. A recurring, cyclical pattern emerged, suggesting that digital literacy, technology-use efficacy, and attitude mutually reinforce one another. These findings highlight the pedagogical value of integrating EduTech tools into process-based English instruction and advocate for instructional models that foster sustainable and reflective digital technology practices.

title_ko: User Perception Dynamics in AI-Based English Learning: A Time-Series Sentiment Analysis of AI PengTalk Reviews
title_en: User Perception Dynamics in AI-Based English Learning: A Time-Series Sentiment Analysis of AI PengTalk Reviews
kw_en: AI PengTalk; user reviews; user perception; time-series sentiment analysis; Orange3
abstract_ko: This study investigated the long-term user perception dynamics of AI PengTalk, an AI-powered English-speaking chatbot, to capture longitudinal insights from spontaneous user feedback. For this purpose, this study employed a time-series sentiment analysis using the VADER model in the Orange3 on 2,351 Google Play user reviews collected over five years (2020-2025). The analysis focused on overall sentiment distribution, temporal changes in user perception, and specific areas for improvement of AI PengTalk. The findings revealed a sustained predominance of positive sentiment over negative sentiment. This positive pattern was not merely initial enthusiasm but remained stable even during a period of dramatic user expansion in 2023. While aligning with technical issues like voice recognition, the analysis also uncovered user frustrations regarding account management and negative pedagogical implementations. The findings validate the key educational value of AI PengTalk while providing a development roadmap for issues mentioned by users. Furthermore, this study demonstrates the methodological value of sentiment analysis as a complementary tool for authentic and dynamic English program evaluation.

title_ko: 인공지능 및 메타버스 기반 국제협력 교사교육 프로그램에 대한 한국 초등영어 예비교사의 경험과 인식
title_en: Korean pre-service elementary English teachers’ experiences and perceptions of an AI- and metaverse-based international collaborative teacher education program
kw_ko: 인공지능; 메타버스; 국제협력 프로그램; 예비교사; 제2언어교사교육
kw_en: artificial intelligence; metaverse; international collaboration program; pre-service teachers; second language teacher education
abstract_ko: This study examines an AI- and metaverse-based international collaborative teacher education program by analyzing Korean pre-service English teachers’ experiences and perceptions. The program, jointly implemented by universities in Korea and Hong Kong, involved 33 participants, including 14 Korean pre-service teachers. Over four weeks, participants engaged in eight hours of regular class sessions and also conducted additional group meetings to collaborate on their projects. Divided into five groups, they developed digital storybooks for Indonesian students. Data collected from their pre- and post- surveys and digital storybooks were qualitatively analyzed. Findings indicate that the program enhanced intercultural communicative competence, English communication skills and opportunities, and edutech literacy in AI and metaverse platforms. The program also fostered the participants’ professional identity and attitudes as future teachers. The digital storybooks demonstrated cultural integration, diverse communicative functions, appropriate language use, and educational value. Challenges included limited interaction with international peers, English communication difficulties, technological infrastructure, and time constraints. The study offers meaningful insights into how AI and the metaverse can be integrated into international collaboration programs for pre-service English teachers.

title_ko: AI-Assisted Request Pragmatics of Korean Pre-Service Elementary English Teachers
title_en: AI-Assisted Request Pragmatics of Korean Pre-Service Elementary English Teachers
kw_en: request; speech act; pragmatics; pre-service teacher; AI translator
abstract_ko: This study examines the pragmatic competence of Korean pre-service elementary English teachers when composing requests with AI translation support. Focusing on formal written and spoken contexts, it examines the types of request head acts (RHAs), internal mitigators, and request supportive moves (RSMs) these future teachers employ. Twenty-two freshmen enrolled in a teacher education program completed a discourse-completion task (DCT) including three scenarios: writing a hotel room-upgrade email, making a room-change request at a hotel front desk, and sending a peer-to-peer activity-change message. Responses were coded (CCSARP-based) for RHA type, syntactic and lexical/phrasal downtoners, and RSMs, including their position relative to the RHA. Results show entitlement-sensitive patterning. In high-entitlement situations (room change), participants favored direct query-preparatory RHAs with minimal support. In lower-entitlement peer interactions, they used off-record strategies and heavier mitigation. Upgrade emails. Despite fluent AI-generated English, the pre-service teachers often exhibited mismatches between context and mitigation: over-verbosity in simple requests and under-mitigation in delicate. The study recommends teacher education on entitlement calibration, proportional mitigation, and pre/post-RHA sequencing to support effective co-teaching and technology-mediated collaboration.

title_ko: Pre-Service Elementary Teachers’ Use of Generative AI in English Lesson Planning: AI-Use Behaviors, Perceptions, and Future Use Intention
title_en: Pre-Service Elementary Teachers’ Use of Generative AI in English Lesson Planning: AI-Use Behaviors, Perceptions, and Future Use Intention
kw_en: generative AI; ChatGPT; lesson planning; pre-service elementary teachers; English teacher education
abstract_ko: The present study investigated how pre-service elementary teachers used ChatGPT during an English lesson-planning task and how their reported AI-use behaviors were related to their perceptions of generative AI and intention for future use. The participants were 26 pre-service elementary teachers enrolled at a national university of education. Data were collected through a questionnaire administered via Google Forms during a regular class session, immediately after the ChatGPT-assisted lesson-planning task. The questionnaire assessed self-reported AI-use behaviors, perceptions of generative AI, and future use intention. Results showed that participants engaged with ChatGPT in iterative and reflective ways rather than relying on it as a one-time support tool. ChatGPT was most frequently used during lesson development, particularly for designing classroom activities, followed by lesson introduction and wrap-up, whereas its use for assessment planning and language-level support was relatively limited. The participants also reported active interaction behaviors, including revising and adding prompts, modifying AI-generated outputs, and critically reviewing suggested ideas. Exploratory correlational analyses revealed that specific interactional behaviors—rather than overall frequency of use—were selectively associated with the participants’ perceptions of generative AI and their intention for future use. Overall, the findings suggest the importance of fostering critical and strategic engagement with generative AI in English teacher education.
