title_ko: Thai Secondary School Teachers’ Perceptions of ChatGPT Use in English Education
title_en: Thai Secondary School Teachers’ Perceptions of ChatGPT Use in English Education
kw_en: ChatGPT; Thai EFL context; teacher perceptions; AI assisted language instruction; student writing and critical thinking
abstract_ko: This study investigates Thai secondary school English teachers’ perceptions of ChatGPT in language education, offering context-sensitive insights from an underexplored Southeast Asian EFL context. Using a mixed-methods approach, data were collected from 31 teachers through surveys and five semi-structured interviews. Most participants reported moderate to high levels of familiarity with ChatGPT and recognized its value for lesson planning and grammar support. However, they also expressed concerns about plagiarism, student overreliance, and the potential weakening of critical thinking skills. Despite these reservations, teachers showed cautious openness to integrating ChatGPT into classroom instruction, provided that structured professional development, clear ethical guidelines, and sustained institutional support are available. Participants emphasized the importance of strengthening artificial intelligence (AI) literacy among students and called for clearer policy direction at both institutional and national levels. These perspectives were shaped by Thailand’s exam-oriented education system and persistent digital inequality. Overall, the findings indicate that effective AI adoption in Thai EFL classrooms requires not only pedagogical readiness but also policy coherence and infrastructural equity.

title_ko: Evolving Paradigms of Feedback in Korean EFL Writing: A Critical Synthesis of Theory, Trends, and AI Approaches
title_en: Evolving Paradigms of Feedback in Korean EFL Writing: A Critical Synthesis of Theory, Trends, and AI Approaches
kw_en: feedback research; EFL writing; AI feedback; multimodal feedback
abstract_ko: This study examines the developmental trajectory of feedback research in Korean EFL writing from the early 1990s to 2025 through a qualitative systematic synthesis of KCI-indexed journal articles. Drawing on major learning theories and educational reforms, the study identifies four stages that reflect shifts in curriculum policy, assessment practices, and the gradual incorporation of digital and AI-based tools. Early work was characterized by teacher-centered and form-focused corrective feedback, followed by comparative studies of feedback types influenced by sociocultural theory and formative assessment perspectives. Recent research has increasingly addressed learners’ metacognition, self-regulation, feedback uptake, and AI-mediated practices. Despite these broader theoretical orientations, the literature remains dominated by short-term interventions and perception-based studies, with limited evidence on sustained writing development in classroom settings. The findings indicate a gap between theoretical advancement and instructional practice in Korean EFL writing. This study calls for longitudinal, classroom-based, and mixed-method research that examines how teacher-, peer-, and AI-mediated feedback can be integrated within context-sensitive instructional models.

title_ko: Effects of AI-Restricted English Discussion Class on Self-Directed Learning at University
title_en: Effects of AI-Restricted English Discussion Class on Self-Directed Learning at University
kw_ko: 영어교육에서의 인공지능; 자기주도학습; 인공지능제한수업; 인지적 주도권; 학습자 인식
kw_en: artificial intelligence in English education; self-directed learning; AI-restricted instruction; cognitive agency; learner perception
abstract_ko: The rapid proliferation of Generative AI (GenAI) in higher education has introduced significant benefits but also caused widespread cognitive offloading, potentially eroding learner agency. As an exploratory study utilizing a small-scale sample (N=23), this research investigates the impact of an AI-restricted English discussion environment on university students’ self-directed learning (SDL) and their perceptions of critical agency and course satisfaction. Employing a 10-week intervention that prohibited AI access during spontaneous communication, the study sought to enforce cognitive onloading and pushed output. Paired-samples t-tests revealed statistically significant improvements across all five SDL sub-factors, most notably in autonomy (t=-9.23) and self-concept (t=-8.19). These results confirm that AI restriction functions as a desirable difficulty, compelling students to navigate the struggles of lexical/syntactic formulation during discussion. Qualitative analysis further revealed that learners viewed the restriction as a necessary pedagogical measure for fostering critical thinking skills (82.6% positive). Furthermore, 86.9% of participants expressed a desire for future AI-restricted courses. These findings advocate for a ‘strategic hybrid model’ in university curricula, where ‘AI-free zones’ are intentionally designated during production phases to reclaim cognitive agency and foster intrinsic motivation.

title_ko: ChatGPT를 활용한 프랑스어 요약하기활동 수업 사례 연구
title_en: Étude de cas pédagogique sur des activités de résumé en français à l’aide de ChatGPT
kw_ko: 요약하기; 활용 양상; 학습자 인식; 학습 보조 도구
kw_en: ChatGPT; résumé; modalités d’usage; perception des apprenants; outil d’aide à l’apprentissage
abstract_ko: 본 연구는 프랑스어 전공 학습자를 대상으로 ChatGPT를 활용한 요약하기 활동의 수업 사례를 제시하고, ChatGPT 활용 양상 및 학습자 인식을 분석하는 것을 목적으로 한다. 수업은 전통적 읽기 중심의 사전 활동과 ChatGPT를 활용한 텍스트 수정 및 요약 중심의 본 활동으로 구성되었다. 요약문을 수정하는 짝 활동에서 학습자들은 수정 항목별 설명, 한국어 번역, 분량 확인 등을 요청하며 요약문을 보완하였다. 일부 학습자는 ChatGPT를 활용해 수정한 요약문이 아닌 다른 결과물을 제출하였는데, 이러한 양상은 학습자들이 요약하고 ChatGPT를 활용해 수정하는 동안 텍스트를 반복해서 읽고 분석하면서 중심 내용을 파악하는 능력이 강화되었음을 시사한다. 개인 활동으로 진행된 요약하기 활동에서는 프랑스어 텍스트를 제시한 뒤 작성 언어, 분량, 포함 내용 등의 조건을 추가하며 산출물을 조정하는 양상이 확인되었다. 본 연구를 통해 학습자들이 ChatGPT를 자기주도적으로 활용하는 한편, 생성 내용에 오류가 포함될 수 있음을 인지하고 있다는 사실을 알 수 있었다. 또한 ChatGPT가 프랑스어 요약하기 활동에서 보조 도구로 활용될 수 있음을 확인할 수 있었다.
abstract_en: Cette étude a pour objectif de présenter un cas pédagogique sur des activités de résumé en français intégrant l’usage de ChatGPT auprès d’apprenants spécialisés en français, et d’analyse à la fois les modalités d’utilisation de l’outil et la perception des étudiants. Lors de l’activité de révision en binôme, les apprenants ont amélioré leur texte en sollicitant, entre autres, des explications sur les points à corriger, des traductions en coréen ainsi que des vérifications de la longueur. Dans l’activité individuelle de production de résumé, les apprenants ont fourni un texte en français et ont ajusté les propositions de ChatGPT en précisant des contraintes telles que la langue de rédaction, la longueur attendue ou les éléments à inclure. Les analyses montrent que les apprenants mobilisent ChatGPT dans une démarche d’apprentissage autodirigé, tout en restant conscients du risque d’erreurs dans les contenus générés. Cette étude met en évidence que les apprenants utilisent ChatGPT de manière autonome tout en étant conscients des limites des contenus générés, et confirme également que ChatGPT peut être mobilisé comme outil d’appui dans des activités de résumé en français.

title_ko: 생성형 AI 챗봇과 메타버스 기반 영어 역사 수업 설계와 학습 경험 분석 연구
title_en: Reimagining History of English Instruction through Generative AI Chatbots and the Metaverse
kw_ko: 영어사 교육; 메타버스 기반 학습; 생성형 AI 챗봇; 프로젝트 기반 학습; 디지털 리터러시; 생성형 인공지능
kw_en: English History education; Metaverse-based learning; Generative AI chatbots; Project-based learning; Digital literacy; Generative AI
abstract_ko: Traditionally, teaching history of English often relies on lecture-based explanations of linguistic change, which limits learners’ opportunities to experience language within its historical and sociocultural contexts. This study explores the pedagogical potential of integrating metaverse and generative AI chatbot technology into teaching history of English. To this end, this study explores the experiences of 37 undergraduate students working on the creation of metaverse spaces with AI chatbots introducing the crucial events, figures and linguistic features according to the development of English. Through an in-depth analysis of its results and students’ reflective reports, this study reveals that students transformed historical timelines into immersive spatial designs and used chatbots as instructional mediators (e.g., historical figures, quiz guides, or language-change explainers). The project fostered digital, prompt, and design literacies and shifted English history learning from memorization toward contextualized, meaning-oriented understanding. The findings suggest that combining metaverse environments with generative AI can effectively support experiential and creative approaches to History of English education.

title_en: A comparative study of the relationship between error analysis and assessment results in college students’ English writing: A comparison of ChatGPT and native English teachers
kw_ko: 영어교육; 영어작문; 오류분석; 평가; 챗지피티
kw_en: English education; English writing; error analysis; assessment; ChatGPT
abstract_ko: This study examined differences between ChatGPT and native English-speaking teachers in erroranalysis and writing assessment of English learner compositions, and explored the relationshipbetween error analysis and assessment outcomes. Twenty-seven college English learnersparticipated in the study, and Pearson correlation, multiple regression analysis, and one-wayANOVA were conducted. The results showed that ChatGPT and the teachers shared a broadlysimilar framework for recognizing learner errors, but differed in the scope and focus of erroridentification. While both displayed comparable tendencies in ‘language-use’ errors, ChatGPTidentified a greater number of errors in ‘content’, ‘organization’, and ‘vocabulary’ based onbroader, macro-level criteria, whereas the teachers identified more errors in ‘writing technique’. Inwriting assessment, no significant differences were found in surface-level linguistic domains;however, a significant difference emerged between ChatGPT and one native English teacher in‘content’ and ‘organization’. Finally, error frequency was not applied as a uniform penalty factorby either ChatGPT and the teachers, suggesting that assessment outcomes depended more on howevaluators interpreted and incorporated errors within their evaluative perspectives. Pedagogicalimplications and directions of further research were discussed.

title_ko: The Role of Model Prompts and Feedback Seeking Behavior in ChatGPT-Assisted EFL Writing
title_en: The Role of Model Prompts and Feedback Seeking Behavior in ChatGPT-Assisted EFL Writing
authors: 안효영(이화여자대학교); Patricia Angelina(Ewha Womans University); Josephine Mijin Lee(Ewha Womans University)
kw_en: generative artificial intelligence; L2 writing; prompt design; corrective feedback; feedback seeking behavior
abstract_ko: The increasing use of generative AI (Gen-AI) tools in education is attracting scholarly attention, particularly regarding their impact on second language (L2) writing development. While Gen-AI provides cognitive and motivational support, concerns persist about overreliance and diminished learner autonomy. This study examines how prompt design affects the quality of AI-assisted writing revisions and learners’ feedback seeking behavior (FSB), which serves as an indicator of learner agency. Forty-three undergraduate EFL students were randomly assigned to one of two conditions: a direct feedback model prompt (DMP) or an indirect feedback model prompt (IMP). After writing initial drafts independently, participants revised their work using ChatGPT. The results indicated significant improvement within-group, especially in language use and vocabulary. Although there were no statistically significant differences in revised-draft scores between the groups, the DMP group performed better in mechanics and language use, with small to moderate effect sizes. Regarding FSB, while group differences were not statistically significant, effect size analysis showed that the DMP group was more engaged in seeking feedback. These findings suggest that prompt design can influence learner-AI interactions and enhance learner agency, providing valuable insights for integrating Gen-AI tools into L2 writing instruction.

title_ko: A Case Study of Korean English Teachers’ Use of AI Digital Textbooks in Elementary Schools
title_en: A Case Study of Korean English Teachers’ Use of AI Digital Textbooks in Elementary Schools
kw_ko: case study / AI 디지털교과서(AIDT); 초등영어교사; 목적 표집; 사례 연구
kw_en: AI Digital Textbook; elementary English teacher; purposeful sampling
abstract_ko: This study explores how two Korean female English teachers integrated an AI Digital Textbook (AIDT) into their Grade 4 classrooms in South Korea. One teacher used AIDT for a semester, while the other implemented it over a year. Data were gathered through semi-structured individual interviews with the teachers, along with lesson plans, school reports, parent surveys, and photographs of classroom activities. These diverse sources were triangulated and member-checked to enhance validity. Content analysis was used to interpret the data. The teachers employed different strategies with AIDT, which shaped both the challenges and benefits they experienced. Initially, students faced technical difficulties logging in, which increased the teachers’ emotional workload. Additionally, some students felt anxious due to ‘negative’ automated feedback emphasizing accuracy in speaking, leading to reluctance in participating in speaking activities. Ironically, while AIDT offered individualized learning experiences and automated assessment, it also diminished human interaction between teachers and students. Based on these findings, the study recommends that teachers actively mediate and reinterpret AIDT feedback and advocates for redesigning AIDT to better promote collaborative language use. Ultimately, the study highlights the importance of incorporating English teachers’ experiences and insights into the development of AIDT.

title_ko: 초등 예비교사의 AI 활용 스토리북 기반 영어교재 개작 연구
title_en: A study of pre-service elementary teachers’ AI-assisted adaptation of storybook-based English teaching materials.
kw_ko: AI 기반 교재개발; 영어 스토 리북 개작; 초등영어교육; 구문 복잡성; 담화 응집성
kw_en: AI-assisted material development; elementary English education; syntactic complexity; discourse cohesion
abstract_ko: This study compared pre-service elementary teachers’ direct and AI-assisted adaptations of English storybooks to identify effective strategies for designing storybook-based English reading materials. Although authentic storybooks provide meaningful input for young EFL learners, they are often linguistically demanding and require careful adaptation. However, adapting texts to learners’ developmental levels requires considerable pedagogical expertise and time. While generative AI tools such as ChatGPT offer practical support for material development, empirical validation of AI-assisted adaptations remains limited. To address this gap, the study analyzed adapted texts quantitatively using three computational linguistic tools(TAALES, TAASSC, TAACO)and qualitatively through surveys, reflective reports, and interviews with pre-service teachers. The findings showed that both teacher-led and AI-assisted adaptations maintained appropriate lexical frequency and overall syntactic complexity. However, teacher adaptations relied more on lexical repetition and meaning-based cohesion, while more actively reflecting learners’ experiences and educational values. In contrast, ChatGPT-generated texts demonstrated greater structural diversity, linguistic accuracy, and efficiency, but they showed limited contextual and pedagogical sensitivity. This study underscores that teachers should remain the central agents of pedagogical judgment, with AI functioning as a complementary support tool in developing learner-centered English reading materials in elementary classrooms.

title_ko: Operationalizing AI in Primary English Classrooms: A Thematic Qualitative Synthesis of AI PengTalk Application
title_en: Operationalizing AI in Primary English Classrooms: A Thematic Qualitative Synthesis of AI PengTalk Application
kw_ko: AI 펭톡
kw_en: AI chatbot; AI PengTalk; operationalization; thematic qualitative synthesis
abstract_ko: This study investigates the pedagogical mechanisms underlying the integration of ‘AI PengTalk,’ a government-initiated AI speaking practice system, into South Korean primary English education. To address the gap in understanding its classroom operationalization, a thematic qualitative synthesis of 36 empirical studies was conducted. Instructional models, learner affordances and perceptions, and teacher and peer mediation strategies in response to technological and assessment constraints were systematically analyzed. The findings reveal that AI PengTalk is most prominently operationalized within Flipped Learning, Spaced Practice, and Differentiated Remedial Instruction models. Pedagogically, the tool creates a ‘psychological safety zone’ that significantly lowers the affective filter for lower-proficiency learners, fostering a sense of social presence and motivation through gamification. However, it simultaneously exhibits a ‘ceiling effect’ and a fading novelty for advanced students due to the lack of sophisticated corrective feedback. Furthermore, technical and assessment constraints —such as speech recognition errors and rigid grading algorithms—necessitate that teachers evolve into active pedagogical mediators who manage learner frustration, supported by peer collaborative scaffolding. The study concludes that successful AI integration does not replace human instruction but requires a restructuring of the teacher’s role to combine high-tech data utilization with high-touch emotional support.

title_ko: 생성형 AI 기반 쓰기 피드백의 효과와 학습자 반응 분석
title_en: Effects of Generative AI–Based Writing Feedback and Learner Responses
kw_ko: 생성형 AI; 쓰기 피드백; 고쳐쓰기; 인간 피드백; 챗지피티
kw_en: Generative AI; writing feedback; revision; human feedback; ChatGPT
abstract_ko: 본 연구에서는 생성형 AI 기반 쓰기 피드백의 교육적 효과와 특성을 검증하기 위해 인간 평가자와 ChatGPT에 의해 산출된 피드백이 고등학생의 논술 답안 고쳐쓰기 성과에 미치는 영향을 비교·분석하였다. 이를 위해 154명의 고등학교 2학년 학생들을 대상으로 준실험적 사전–사후 설계를 적용하여 양적 효과를 분석하고, 학생 인식 설문을 통해 질적 특질을 도출하였다. 분석 결과, AI 피드백의 효과 크기가 인간 피드백에 비해 미세하게 높게 나타났으며, 이원분산분석에서는 쓰기 수준의 주효과만이 유의하게 확인되었다. 질적 분석 결과, AI 피드백은 구체성과 실현 가능성, 체계성과 일관성, 표현 개선 중심이라는 강점을 지니는 반면, 전형성과 메타인지 유도의 한계를 함께 내포하는 것으로 나타났다. 이러한 결과는 생성형 AI 피드백이 1차 수정 도구로 활용될 수 있음을 드러내며, 고차적 논증 요소와 메타인지 유도를 위해서는 교사 피드백과의 혼합 활용이 필요함을 시사한다.
abstract_en: This study compared the effects of feedback generated by human evaluators and ChatGPT on high-school students’ revision performance in argumentative writing to investigate the educational effectiveness and characteristics of generative AI-based writing feedback. A quasi-experimental pretest-posttest design was used with 154 second-year high school students to examine quantitative effects and identify qualitative features through a learner perception survey. The results showed that the effect size of AI feedback was slightly larger than that of human feedback, and the two-way ANOVA revealed a significant main effect only for writing proficiency level. According to qualitative analysis, AI feedback demonstrated strengths in specificity, feasibility, systematicity, consistency, and a focus on improving linguistic expression, but it also had limitations related to stereotypical patterns and insufficient support for metacognitive engagement. These results suggest that generative AI feedback can be used effectively as a tool for initial revision, whereas a hybrid approach that combines it with teacher feedback is required to address higher-order argumentative elements and promote metacognitive processes.
note: 고등생 논술 고쳐쓰기 AI vs 인간 피드백 준실험

title_ko: 수능 ‘언어와 매체’의 단어 문항 풀이에서 나타나는 생성형 인공지능의자연어 설명에 대한 분석
title_en: Surface Fluency and Internal Imperfection in Natural Language Explanations for CSAT “Language and Media” Word Items
kw_ko: 자연어 설명; 표면적 유창성; 내부적 불완전성; 대규모 언어 모델; 생성형 인공지능
kw_en: Natural Language Explanation(NLE); surface fluency; internal imperfection; language model; generative artificial intelligence
abstract_ko: 이 연구의 목적은 대학수학능력시험 ‘언어와 매체’의 단어 관련 문항 풀이와 관련하여 생성형 인공지능이 제공하는 자연어 설명의 특성을 분석하는 것이다. 이 연구는 급속도로 발전하는 인공지능 자연어 처리 기술의 성과를 문법 교육적으로 의미화할 필요성에서 출발하였다. 2022학년도부터 2026학년도까지의 ‘언어와 매체’의 단어 관련 문항을 제미나이 3 프로 모델에 입력하여 자연어 설명을 생성하고 그 특성을 분석하였다. 분석 결과 자연어 설명은 표면적 유창성과 내부적 불완전성의 특성을 가지는 것으로 파악되었다. 표면적 유창성의 양상으로는 문항 구성 요소에 의존하는 출력, 문항에서 주목되는 단서의 활용, 사전 학습된 문법 개념어의 사용을 분석하였다. 내부적 불완전성의 양상으로는 다양한 문항 해결 경로의 생성, 출력 과정에서 오류의 순차적 전달, 사전 학습된 지식의 한계를 기술하였다. 표면적 유창성은 가시적인 반면 내부적 불완전성은 비가시적이기 때문에 문법 교육에서 언어 주체의 비판적인 인식이 중요하게 요구된다.
abstract_en: This study analyzes the characteristics of natural language explanations generated by large language models when solving word-related items in the Korean College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT). Word-related items from the 2022 to 2026 CSAT were input into the Gemini 3 Pro model to generate natural-language explanations, and their features were examined. The analysis indicates that these explanations exhibit two key characteristics: surface fluency and internal imperfection. This study delineates three manifestations of surface fluency: outputs relying on question components, the use of salient cues in the question, and the use of pre-trained grammatical terminology. It also identifies three manifestations of internal imperfections: the generation of multiple solution pathways, the sequential propagation of errors during the output process, and limitations in pre-trained knowledge. Because surface fluency is visible whereas internal error risk is not, grammar education that fosters users’ critical awareness is urgently required.
note: 제미나이 수능 단어 문항 풀이 설명 분석, 문법교육 시사

title_ko: 생성형 AI 활용 글쓰기에서의 대학생 윤리 인식과 교육적 제언
title_en: Patterns of Ethical Awareness in Generative AI-Assisted Writing among University Students and Pedagogical Implications
kw_ko: 생성형 AI; 글쓰기 윤리; AI 윤리; 통합 윤리 교육; 대학 글쓰기; 교양 교육
kw_en: Generative AI; Writing Ethics; AI Ethics; Integrated Ethics Education; College Writing; Liberal Arts Education
abstract_ko: 본 연구는 생성형 AI 활용이 확산된 대학 글쓰기 환경에서 학습자가 글쓰기 윤리를 어떠한 방식으로 인식하는지를 분석하고 이에 기반한 교육적 방향을 제시하는 데 목적이 있다. 대학 글쓰기 수업에서 실시한 설문조사와 조별 ‘생성형 AI 활용 글쓰기 윤리 가이드라인’을 분석하여 대학생의 윤리 인식 양상을 살펴보았다. 분석 결과, 학습자는 생성형 AI 활용 윤리를 가치나 성찰의 문제라기보다 규칙과 지침의 문제로 이해하는 경향을 보였으며 이는 대학 글쓰기 교육이 윤리를 규범 준수 중심으로 다루어 온 교육 환경과도 연관이 있다. 이에 글쓰기 윤리를 외부 규범의 적용이 아니라 글쓰기 과정에서 형성되는 판단의 구조로 이해하고, 제도적 기준, 개인의 책임과 성찰이 상호 작용하도록 설계된 ‘통합 윤리 교육’을 제안하였다. 이러한 접근은 학습자가 생성형 AI 활용 과정에서 윤리 판단과 실천의 주체로 형성될 수 있도록 한다는 점에서 의의를 지닌다.
abstract_en: This study aims to analyze learners’ ethical awareness in writing in the context of generative AI and to propose educational directions based on the findings. To this end, the study examined patterns of ethical awareness among university students by analyzing surveys and group-based “AI Ethics and Writing Guidelines” produced in a university writing course. The results indicate that students tend to perceive the ethics of using generative AI as a matter of rules and guidelines rather than as a matter of values or reflection. Writing ethics, therefore, should be understood not as the application of external norms but as a structure of judgment formed within the writing process itself. Accordingly, this study proposes an “Integrated Ethics Education” model designed to facilitate interaction among institutional standards, individual responsibility, and theoretical reflection. This approach is significant in that it enables learners to develop as agents of ethical judgment and practice in the process of using generative AI.
note: 대학 글쓰기 윤리 인식, 교양교육

title_ko: 교양영어 기반 자유학예 역량교육 혁신모델 개발 연구: CLIL·PBL·생성형 AI를 활용한 Liberal English Track 구축
title_en: Advancing Liberal Arts Education through General English: A CLIL, PBL, and Generative-AI Integrated Liberal English Track Mode
kw_ko: 자유학예영어트랙; 생성형AI문해; 자유학예교육
kw_en: CLIL; PBL; liberal english track; generative AI literacy; liberal arts education
abstract_ko: The rapid expansion of digital technologies, generative AI, and multimodal learning environments has intensified the need to redesign General English so that it functions not merely as a language-skills course but as an entry point into liberal arts education. Recent studies highlight that technology-enhanced English learning, flipped learning, CLIL, PBL, and AI-mediated literacy practices significantly influence students’ engagement, cultural understanding, and higher-order thinking. Against this backdrop, this study proposes a Liberal English Track that integrates CLIL, PBL, and generative-AI strategies to reconstruct General English as a foundation for liberal arts competencies. The research analyzes domestic findings on General English innovation, liberal arts theory, and AI-assisted learning, while examining institutional models such as East Asia University’s “Yungseok Project.” Methodologically, it combines conceptual analysis, curriculum modeling, and evaluation design to build an integrated instructional and assessment framework. The results suggest that CLIL supports interdisciplinary content learning, PBL fosters inquiry and collaborative problem-solving, and generative AI strengthens critical literacy, rhetorical structuring, and self-regulated learning. These components merge to form a coherent Liberal English Track that bridges language, cognition, culture, and academic inquiry. The study concludes that this model can enhance core liberal arts capacities—reasoning, interpretation, communication, and cultural understanding—while providing a scalable foundation for Bachelor of Liberal Arts (BLA) programs and institution-wide CQI-based quality management.

title_ko: Developing AI-Enhanced TPACK: Vietnamese Pre-service EFL Teachers' Integration of ChatGPT in Language Education
title_en: Developing AI-Enhanced TPACK: Vietnamese Pre-service EFL Teachers' Integration of ChatGPT in Language Education
authors: Pham Minh Toan(Ho Chi Minh University of Banking); Le Thi Thuy Nhung(Ho Chi Minh University of Banking)
kw_en: AI-TPACK framework; ChatGPT integration; pre-service EFL teachers; Vietnam
abstract_ko: This study investigates Vietnamese pre-service EFL teachers' readiness for ChatGPT integration through the AI-enhanced TPACK framework. The research addresses two questions: (RQ1) How do Vietnamese pre-service EFL teachers' perceptions and readiness align with AI-enhanced TPACK requirements? (RQ2) What culturally responsive implementation strategies do they plan for ChatGPT integration? Employing an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design, data were collected from 247 pre-service teachers via questionnaires, followed by semi-structured interviews with 12 participants selected through maximum variation sampling. Statistical analysis revealed significant disparities between Content Knowledge (M=5.82) and Pedagogical Knowledge (M=5.64) versus Technology Knowledge (M=4.93). Factor analysis identified four primary barriers: technical infrastructure, institutional support, professional development, and time constraints, explaining 72.4% of implementation challenges. While 83.7% intended to use ChatGPT for instructional planning, correlation analysis showed integration intentions were moderated by institutional support (ΔR²=.14, p<.001) and self-efficacy (β=.53, p<.001). Qualitative findings revealed hybrid implementation approaches emphasizing preparatory rather than real-time use, with cultural adaptation as a central concern. The study demonstrates that successful ChatGPT integration in Vietnamese EFL contexts requires addressing both technical competencies and culturally responsive pedagogical applications.

title_ko: Integrating Generative AI into English Learning: Insights from Korean University EFL Students
title_en: Integrating Generative AI into English Learning: Insights from Korean University EFL Students
authors: 이용직(창원대학교); Robert O. Davis(전남대학교); Jungin Choi
kw_en: AI; GenAI; ELT; higher education; EFL
abstract_ko: This study investigates Korean university EFL students' first-hand experiences, perceptions, and attitudes toward the use of generative AI (GenAI) in English learning. A descriptive survey was administered to 73 undergraduates enrolled in compulsory English courses. Results showed that ChatGPT (65.8%) and Google Translate (42.5%) were the most frequently used tools, primarily for coursework and convenience. Although students generally perceived GenAI as moderately effective for improving English skills, many reported limited familiarity and only moderate technological readiness. Over half of the participants indicated they had never received formal training on using AI tools for language learning. Students rated real-time feedback, translation support, and access to diverse learning resources as key opportunities. These findings suggest that Korean universities should provide structured AI literacy instruction to support pedagogically meaningful and responsible GenAI use in EFL programs, particularly within large, mixed-proficiency general English courses.

title_ko: A Comparative Study of ChatGPT-Based Self-Feedback and Offline Teacher Feedback in EFL Writing: Learner Perceptions
title_en: A Comparative Study of ChatGPT-Based Self-Feedback and Offline Teacher Feedback in EFL Writing: Learner Perceptions
kw_en: ChatGPT-based self-feedback; teacher feedback; process-oriented writing; learners’ perceptions; prompts
abstract_ko: This study examined EFL university learners’ perceptions of ChatGPT-based self-feedback in comparison with teacher feedback, with a focus on proficiency-level differences. Participants were first-year university students categorized into lower-level (n=137) and intermediate-level (n=50) groups. Adopting a mixed-methods approach, the study analyzed learners’ perceptions, feedback preferences, and prompt patterns of interaction with ChatGPT in a process-oriented writing context. The findings indicated that learners in both proficiency groups held positive perceptions of both ChatGPT-based feedback and teacher feedback. Across groups, the immediacy and convenience of ChatGPT feedback were identified as its key strengths, supporting efficient revision and sustained engagement in the writing process. Also, intermediate-level learners showed a stronger preference for teacher feedback, valuing instructors’ expert and discourse-level guidance. In contrast, lower-level learners preferred a combination of ChatGPT-based feedback and teacher feedback, reflecting a support that integrates immediate AI assistance with authoritative human input. Analysis of ChatGPT prompts revealed that learners predominantly relied on the tool for local-level linguistic support, such as grammar correction and sentence refinement, rather than for higher-order writing functions. Moreover, the effectiveness of AI-based feedback was found to depend on learners’ metacognitive awareness and prompt-design skills.

title_ko: 생성형 인공지능 활용 영어 학습이 학습자의 학업성취도와 인공지능에 대한 효용성 인식에 미치는 영향
title_en: Impact of generative artificial intelligence-based English learning on Students' achievement and perceptions of artificial intelligence utility

abstract_ko: 이 연구는 생성형 인공지능 활용 영어 학습이 대학생의 학업성취도와 인공지능에 대한 효용성 인식에 미치는 영향을 조사하였다. 이를 위해 대학교 간호학과 1학년 학생 210명을 생성형 인공지능을 활용하여 수업 활동을 진행한 실험그룹과 교수자의 설명 및 질의응답 중심으로 수업 활동을 진행한 통제그룹으로 나누어 25년 9월부터 10주간 연구를 진행하였다. 연구 결과, 첫째, 실험그룹은 생성형 인공지능 활용 후 영어 학습에 있어서 인공지능의 효용성에 대한 인식에서 통계적으로 유의미한 긍정적인 인식 변화를 보였다. 둘째, 학업성취도 면에서 두 그룹 모두 사전 대비 사후 점수가 유의하게 향상되었으나, 그룹 간 성취도 차이는 통계적으로 유의하지 않았다. 이는 생성형 인공지능이 교수자의 개별 피드백에 준하는 학습 촉진 효과를 제공할 수 있음을 시사한다.
abstract_en: This study investigated the impact of generative artificial intelligence-based English learning on university students' academic achievement and perceptions of artificial intelligence utility. For this purpose, 210 first-year nursing students at a university were divided into an experimental group that conducted class activities using generative artificial intelligence and a control group that conducted class activities through instructor-led explanations and question-and-answer sessions. The study was carried out for 10 weeks starting in September 2025. The results showed that, first, the experimental group showed statistically significant positive changes in their perceptions of artificial intelligence utility on English learning after using generative artificial intelligence. Second, in terms of academic achievement, both groups significantly improved their scores compared to the pre-test, but the difference in academic achievement between the groups was not statistically significant. This suggests that generative artificial intelligence can provide learning promotion effects comparable to individual feedback from an instructor.

abstract_ko: 4차 산업혁명과 함께 에듀테크가 교육의 필수 요소로 자리 잡았으나, 기존의 AI 기반 언어 학습 도구는 영어 등 주요 언어에 편중되어 있어 러시아어와 같은 특수 외국어 학습자들은 기술적 혜택에서 소외되어 왔다. 이에 본 연구는 러시아어 학습자를 위한 ‘AI 챗봇 기반 맞춤형 학습 시스템’ 개발을 제안하고 그 교육적 효과를 고찰하는 데 목적이 있다. 본 연구에서 제안하는 시스템은 거대 언어 모델(LLM)인 GPT를 기반으로 문맥에 적합한 자연스러운 대화를 생성하며, 음성 인식(STT) 및 합성(TTS) 기술을 결합하여 텍스트와 음성을 아우르는 통합적 학습 환경을 제공한다. 또한 학습자의 오류 데이터를 분석하여 취약점을 진단하고 맞춤형 콘텐츠를 추천하는 알고리즘을 통해 기존 단순 암기식 학습의 한계를 극복하고자 하였다. 연구 결과, AI 챗봇 시스템은 학습자에게 원어민과의 대화와 유사한 실감 나는 학습 경험을 제공함으로써 러시아어 특유의 복잡한 굴절과 발음 난이도를 극복하는 데 기여함을 확인하였다. 이는 전문 교수자 부족이나 지리적 한계를 겪는 학습자들에게 교육 기회를 확대하고 자기 주도적 학습 능력을 신장시키는 데 중요한 역할을 할 것으로 기대된다. 마지막으로 본 연구는 향후 과제로 언어권별 특화된 프롬프트 가이드라인 개발, AI 활용 윤리 규정의 제도화, 장기적 종단 연구의 수행, 그리고 과정 중심 평가 체계로의 전환을 제언한다.
abstract_en: This paper proposes a study on the development of an AI chatbot learning tool specifically for learners of the Russian language. With the advent of the Fourth Industrial Revolution, Edutech has established itself as an essential element of education rather than a mere option. In particular, amidst the trends of ‘digital literacy’and ‘AI-based personalized learning’emphasized in the 2022 Revised National Curriculum, the field of foreign language education is actively adopting AI technology. However, current AI-based language learning tools are predominantly concentrated on major languages such as English, leaving learners of Critical Foreign Languages, including Russian, marginalized from these technological benefits. Accordingly, this study proposes the development of an ‘AI Chatbot-based Personalized Learning System’for Russian learners. The proposed system aims to generate natural, context-appropriate dialogue based on GPT, a Large Language Model (LLM), and to provide an integrated learning environment encompassing both text and speech by combining Speech-to-Text (STT) and Text-to-Speech (TTS) technologies. Furthermore, by designing algorithms that analyze learner error data to diagnose weaknesses and recommend personalized content, this study seeks to overcome the limitations of existing rote-memorization learning applications. The findings of this study demonstrate that the AI chatbot system offers learners an experience similar to conversing with a native speaker and contributes to overcoming the difficulties associated with Russian's complex inflectional morphology and pronunciation. This plays a crucial role in expanding educational opportunities and enhancing self-directed learning capabilities for learners who face challenges in accessing high-quality Russian education due to a shortage of instructors or geographical constraints. In conclusion, this study is significant in that it presents a new paradigm for second foreign language education by converging humanistic linguistic knowledge with the latest IT technology. Based on the results of this study, the following suggestions are made for future Russian language education and follow-up research: First, the development of AI utilization manuals and prompts specialized for specific language groups is urgent. Current AI models are often trained on English-based data, which can lead to case declension errors or unnatural vocabulary choices when generating Slavic languages, including Russian. Therefore, to enable Russian major learners to obtain more precise responses, ‘optimized prompt guidelines’tailored to grammar levels and situations should be developed and disseminated to the educational field. Second, the institutionalization of guidelines for research ethics and plagiarism prevention is necessary. As reliance on AI in completing assignments increases, citation regulations must be clearly established so that learners can distinguish between their own ideas and AI-generated outputs. Departments or academic societies should concretize the allowable scope of Generative AI usage and ethical guidelines to induce learners to recognize AI as a learning aid rather than a tool for academic dishonesty. Third, there is a need for long-term longitudinal studies. This study is limited in that it measured short-term effects over a single semester (or a specific period). To verify the long-term impact of AI utilization on learners’actual language acquisition and on maintaining continuous learning motivation after the initial interest subsides, follow-up research spanning more than one year should be conducted. Fourth, innovation in assessment methods is suggested. Product-oriented assessment is losing its discriminatory power due to the advancement of AI technology. Therefore, a transition to a multifaceted evaluation system is required, such as ‘process-oriented assessment’that evaluates the process of learners interacting with AI and refining the results, or expanding the proportion of oral interviews and on-site writing assessments.

title_en: The educational effects of an AI-based TOEIC reading course at the university level
kw_ko: AI 학습; 챗GPT; 영어독해; 대학생 인식; 토익읽기; 학습일지
kw_en: AI learning; ChatGPT; English reading comprehension; college students’ perceptions; TOEIC reading; learning journal
abstract_ko: This study investigated the educational impact of an AI-based TOEIC reading course at the university level, with a particular focus on AI-assisted learning journal writing. It examined changes in students' TOEIC reading achievement and explored their perceptions, emotional attitudes, and satisfaction regarding AI-integrated instruction. The participants included 58 first-year university students enrolled in a TOEIC reading course, who were divided into an experimental group using AI-assisted journals and a control group using traditional journals. Analysis of pre- and post-test TOEIC reading scores was conducted, along with survey questionnaires and interviews. The results showed a statistically significant improvement in TOEIC reading scores within the experimental group. However, no significant difference was found in post-test performance between the experimental and control groups. Survey results indicated that learners found AI-assisted learning journals beneficial for understanding sentences and paragraphs, completing assignments, and promoting self-directed learning. Participants also reported generally positive emotional responses, including reduced anxiety and increased psychological comfort. These findings suggest that AI-assisted learning journals can enhance individual reading development and contribute to positive learning experiences in TOEIC reading instruction.

title_ko: Comparing the Effectiveness of Two Machine Translation-Based Instructional Models for English Writing
title_en: Comparing the Effectiveness of Two Machine Translation-Based Instructional Models for English Writing
kw_en: machine translation; Google Translate; English writing instruction; instructional models
abstract_ko: The present study employed a mixed-methods research design to compare the effectiveness of two machine translation (MT)-integrated instructional models for English writing and to examine students’ perceptions of each model. A total of 47 university students enrolled in two sections of an English for Academic Purposes (EAP) writing course participated in the study. The two models differed in the instructional role of Google Translate. Model 1 utilized back-translation (English → Korean) to help students identify discrepancies between their intended meaning and translated output, thereby supporting error detection and revision. Model 2 allowed students to selectively use Google Translate (Korean → English) at the word, phrase, and sentence levels to assist with linguistic production during the revision process. Three research questions were investigated and the results can be summarized as follows. First, a t-test showed no statistically significant difference in effectiveness between the two models. Second, a Kruskal–Wallis test showed no significant differences in perceived usefulness across English proficiency levels, indicating that instructional designs tailored to English proficiency may not be necessary in this context. Third, students also perceived back-translation as particularly useful for identifying vocabulary errors, and views on its usefulness for grammar correction were divergent. This study provides pedagogical implications for designing MT-integrated writing instruction in similar EAP courses.

title_ko: 주의집중 기반 언어모델의 구조적 차이에 따른 자동화 영어 에세이 다면평가 양상의 비교 분석
title_en: A comparative study of automated multi-trait English essay scoring across attention-based language model architectures
kw_ko: 자동화 에세이 평가; 언어모델; 주의집중; 에세이 다면평가; 인공지능
kw_en: Automated essay scoring; language model; attention; multi-trait essay scoring; artificial intelligence
abstract_ko: Recent advances in attention-based language models have increased interest in automated essay scoring (AES) for English essays, particularly analytic scoring. However, prior work has primarily focused on improving score agreement with human raters, with limited attention to how different model architectures realize analytic assessment from an educational perspective. Accordingly, this study examines how architectural differences in attention-based language models influence analytic English essay scoring by comparing encoder-based (BERT), decoder-based (Qwen), and encoder–decoder-based (T5) models on the PERSUADE 1.0 dataset, consisting of essays written by U.S. students in grades 8–12 and rated by two trained raters, with final scores determined through adjudication by a third rater. The analysis evaluates agreement with human raters using Quadratic Weighted Kappa (QWK), attention patterns by classifying attention-weighted tokens into content and function words via part-of-speech tagging, and scoring efficiency by measuring average inference time per essay under both CPU and GPU environments. The results show that the encoder– decoder-based (T5) model achieves the highest agreement with human raters by focusing more on content words, reflecting a meaning-focused assessment strategy. In contrast, other models show lower agreement with less emphasis on content words. Despite moderate computational costs, the encoder–decoder-based model remains feasible for educational use. These findings highlight the importance of model architecture in analytic AES and offer guidance for selecting practical scoring systems.

title_ko: A Multi-Phase Developmental Analysis of EFL University Students’ Complexity, Accuracy, and Fluency through ChatGPT-Mediated Speaking Tasks
title_en: A Multi-Phase Developmental Analysis of EFL University Students’ Complexity, Accuracy, and Fluency through ChatGPT-Mediated Speaking Tasks
kw_en: ChatGPT/GenAI/CAF/multi-phase developmental study/learner corpus/EFL speaking
abstract_ko: Framed by the interaction between two competing theoretical perspectives within the complexity, accuracy, and fluency (CAF) framework—the limited attention capacity hypothesis and the cognition hypothesis— this multi-phase developmental study investigates the incremental patterns of linguistic growth among 32 Korean university EFL learners engaging in ChatGPT-mediated speaking tasks over a seven-week period. Utilizing a learner corpus derived from sequential AI-interactive sessions, the study analyzed the linguistic growth across three temporal phases (T1, T2, and T3) using one-way repeated measures ANOVA. Research findings are as follows: 1) Complexity (MLT, C/T) showed a significant linear upward trend. 2) Accuracy (EFT/T) ratio exhibited a distinct U-shaped pattern, where an initial decline during the mid-phase was followed by a significant rebound by the final stage. 3) Fluency (WPT) revealed a steady increase, with significant acceleration occurring in the later phase as task demands went up. These findings suggest that generative AI (GenAI) provides language learners with digital scaffolding, encouraging them to make more output within a low-anxiety environment while facilitating the use of complex linguistic structures. This study concludes with pedagogical implications and research limitations.

title_ko: ChatGPT 를 활용한 과정 중심의 영작문 수업 모형에 대한 학생들의 인식 탐색
title_en: Students’ perceptions of a process-oriented English writing instruction model using ChatGPT
kw_ko: 영어 쓰기 수업/챗지피티/인식
kw_en: English Writing Instruction /ChatGPT /Perceptions
abstract_ko: This study investigates university students’ perceptions of and satisfaction with a process oriented English writing instruction model using ChatGPT. The study systematically integrated ChatGPT into multiple stages of the writing process, including revising, editing, and reflective activities. Data were collected through pre- and post-questionnaires on students’ perceptions, along with open-ended survey responses. The results indicate that students demonstrated high levels of satisfaction with the ChatGPT-assisted writing course and held positive perceptions of ChatGPT as a supportive writing tool rather than a writing substitute. Students valued ChatGPT’s role in improving grammatical accuracy, naturalness of expression, and efficiency in revision and editing. While students expressed concerns about potential overreliance on ChatGPT, they generally recognized its educational benefits when used critically and strategically. Regarding learner background variables, nonparametric analyses revealed no significant differences in perceptions by overall English proficiency, whereas writing proficiency and TOEIC scores were associated with differential views on the usefulness of ChatGPT, with lower-proficiency learners reporting greater reliance on ChatGPT for idea generation and revision and higher-proficiency learners emphasizing the need for explicit guidance and ethical use. These findings suggest that integrating ChatGPT into writing instruction can foster learners’ engagement in the writing process and support effective and responsible use of generative tools when accompanied by explicit pedagogical guidance.

title_ko: ChatGPT 활용 영어 쓰기 활동에서 나타난 중학생의 정의적 요인 변화와 자기주도성 수준에 따른 반응 차이
title_en: Changes in middle school students’ affective factors in ChatGPT-assisted English writing: Differences by levels of self-directedness
kw_ko: ChatGPT 활용 쓰기; 정의적 요인; 자기주도성; 영어 쓰기; AI 활용 학습
kw_en: ChatGPT-assisted Writing; Affective Factors; Self-directedness; EFL Writing; AI-assisted Learning
abstract_ko: This study examined changes in middle school students’ affective factors during ChatGPT-assisted English writing activities and explored whether responses differed according to levels of self-directedness. Seventy second-grade students participated in a short-term writing program in which ChatGPT was used as a support tool during English writing tasks. Pre- and post-surveys measured four affective variables: learning motivation, interest, anxiety, and self-efficacy, as well as students’ levels of self-directedness. Quantitative data were analyzed using paired-samples t-tests, independent-samples t-tests, and correlation analysis, complemented by qualitative data from open-ended responses and interviews. The results showed significant increases in learning motivation, interest, and self-efficacy after the activities, while anxiety did not change significantly. When students were divided into higher and lower self-directedness groups, both groups demonstrated positive changes in affective factors, although differences in the magnitude of change were not statistically significant. Qualitative findings indicated that students with higher self-directedness emphasized improving expressions and developing ideas, whereas those with lower self-directedness highlighted reduced writing difficulty and easier error correction. Correlation analyses further revealed significant positive relationships between motivation, interest, self-efficacy, and self-directedness. These findings indicate that AI-assisted writing activities are associated with learners’ affective engagement and self-directed participation in EFL writing contexts.

title_ko: The effects of teacher and ChatGPT feedback on uptake and affective attitudes in Korean EFL high school
title_en: The effects of teacher and ChatGPT feedback on uptake and affective attitudes in Korean EFL high school
kw_en: ChatGPT; Written Corrective Feedback(WCF); Uptake; L2 Writing; EFL Learners
abstract_ko: This mixed-methods study, conducted over an eight-week period, investigated the differential effects of ChatGPT-4o and teacher-provided written corrective feedback (WCF) on uptake and affective responses among 62 first-year high school students in Daegu, South Korea. Across three writing-feedback-revision cycles based on Holes, both groups demonstrated significant increases in feedback incorporation. However, the teacher feedback group achieved superior uptake quality, with a clear shift toward deeper, meaning-focused revisions. In contrast, ChatGPT proved particularly effective for rapid surface-level corrections and was associated with a more pronounced reduction in writing anxiety. While teacher feedback elicited larger gains in writing motivation and self-efficacy due to perceived professional credibility and relational care, ChatGPT was valued for providing a low-stakes, non-judgmental environment. These findings suggest that AI-mediated feedback effectively mitigates affective barriers and supports formal accuracy, whereas teacher expertise remains indispensable for fostering cognitive depth and relational engagement in secondary L2 writing contexts.
abstract_en: This mixed-methods study, conducted over an eight-week period, investigated the differential effects of ChatGPT-4o and teacher-provided written corrective feedback (WCF) on uptake and affective responses among 62 first-year high school students in Daegu, South Korea. Across three writing-feedback-revision cycles based on Holes, both groups demonstrated significant increases in feedback incorporation. However, the teacher feedback group achieved superior uptake quality, with a clear shift toward deeper, meaning-focused revisions. In contrast, ChatGPT proved particularly effective for rapid surface-level corrections and was associated with a more pronounced reduction in writing anxiety. While teacher feedback elicited larger gains in writing motivation and self-efficacy due to perceived professional credibility and relational care, ChatGPT was valued for providing a low-stakes, non-judgmental environment. These findings suggest that AI-mediated feedback effectively mitigates affective barriers and supports formal accuracy, whereas teacher expertise remains indispensable for fostering cognitive depth and relational engagement in secondary L2 writing contexts.

title_ko: ChatGPT 피드백과 고등학생 EFL 학습자의 피드백 리터러시: 수능 영어 읽기에서의 학습자 피드백 수용 탐색
title_en: ChatGPT feedback and high school EFL learner feedback literacy in CSAT English reading: A qualitative inquiry
kw_ko: ChatGPT 피드백; 피드백 리터러시; 수능 영어; EFL 읽기 교육; 프롬프트 전략
kw_en: ChatGPT Feedback; Feedback Literacy; CSAT English; EFL Reading Instruction; Prompting Strategy
abstract_ko: This qualitative study explores how Korean high school EFL learners process ChatGPT 5.0-generated feedback during CSAT English reading tasks, grounded in Carless and Boud’s (2018) feedback literacy framework. Ten 10th-graders completed 15 CSAT mock items and revised incorrect responses while interacting with ChatGPT during concurrent think-alouds. Data from think-aloud protocols, interaction logs, and pre-/post-interviews were analyzed across four feedback literacy dimensions: appreciating, judging, managing affect, and taking action. Four key findings emerged. First, higher achievers utilized ChatGPT for metacognitive self-monitoring and strategy reconstruction, while lower achievers experienced cognitive overload and relied on translation assistance. Second, learners perceived ChatGPT feedback as more useful for form- and discourse-focused items than for meaning-focused items. Third, higher achievers employed elaborative prompts, whereas lower achievers defaulted to passive translation requests. Fourth, affective responses—including self-esteem-based resistance and cognitive fatigue—constrained feedback uptake, with students generally preferring teacher feedback for its contextual and emotional scaffolding. These findings suggest a complementary relationship between ChatGPT and teacher feedback, underscoring the need for systematic AI prompting and feedback literacy instruction in EFL reading classrooms.

title_ko: 대학 교양 영어 수업에서 생성형 AI를 활용한 말하기 및 피드백 활동에 대한 학습자 경험 및 인식 연구
title_en: A Study on Learners’ Experiences and Perceptions of Generative AI-assisted Speaking and Feedback Activities in University General English Course
kw_ko: 생성형 AI; 교양 영어; 대화문 기반 역할극; 피드백; 학습자 인식; 재발화
kw_en: Generative AI; General English; Script-based Role-play; Feedback; Learner Perception; Re-speaking
abstract_ko: 본 연구는 대학 교양 영어 수업 맥락에서 생성형 AI(Gemini)를 활용하여 말하기 및 피드백 활동에 대한 학습자의경험과 인식을 탐색하는 데 목적이 있다. 이를 위해 교양 영어 수강생 37명을 대상으로 8주간 교재 대화문 기반의AI 역할극 말하기 및 피드백 과업을 실시하고, 수집된 자료를 바탕으로 기술통계 및 Spearman 순위 상관분석을 실시하였으며, 개방형 응답에 대한 질적 분석을 병행하였다. 연구 결과는 다음과 같다. 첫째, 학습자들은 AI 피드백 활동을통해 ‘감정과 톤을 반영’한 자연스러운 발화 연습, ‘양면적 피드백’, ‘발음·억양 개선’, ‘향후 지속 사용 의사’ 측면에서긍정적인 인식을 보였으나, '자신감 향상'에 대한 인식은 상대적으로 낮게 나타났다. 특히 상관분석 결과, '흥미도향상'은 1차 설문의 '피드백 활동에 대한 학습적 기대' 및 2차 설문의 '향후 지속 사용 의사'와 가장 강한 정적 상관을나타내어, 내재적 흥미가 AI를 활용한 지속적 학습을 견인하는 요인임을 확인하였다. 둘째, 개방형 응답 분석 결과, AI 말하기 활동의 주요 이점은 '심리적 부담 완화', '구체적 피드백 제공', '흥미 유발'로 도출되었으나, 칭찬 위주의모호한 피드백이나 음성 인식 오류와 같은 기술적 한계, 그리고 비언어적 상호작용의 부재가 제약 요인으로 지적되었다. 본 연구는 학습자가 AI를 단순한 말하기 연습 도구를 넘어 피드백 수용 및 '재발화' 과정에 통합적으로 활용하는경험을 제공하고, 초기 사용자의 인식 양상과 주요 관련 변인 간의 관계를 탐색적으로 파악하였다는 점에서 의의가있다. 이러한 결과는 교과목 설계 시 AI의 기술적 한계를 보완하고 학습자를 안내하는 교수자의 매개적 역할을 강조하며, 향후 AI 연계 교양 영어 교수학습 모형 개발을 위한 기초 자료로 활용될 수 있을 것이다.
abstract_en: This study aimed to explore learners' experiences and perceptions of speaking and feedback activities using generative AI (Gemini) in a university general English course. To this end, 37 students performed script-based AI roleplay and feedback tasks over an eight-week period. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Spearman’s rank correlation analysis, and qualitative thematic analysis of the open-ended responses. The findings are as follows. First, learners demonstrated positive perceptions of AI feedback activities, particularly in terms of "incorporating emotion and tone" for natural delivery, "improvement in pronunciation and intonation," and "continuance intention." However, their perception of "increased confidence" remained relatively low. Notably, correlation analysis revealed that "increased interest" showed the strongest positive correlation with both "educational expectations for feedback activities" from the first survey and "continuance intention" from the second survey, confirming that intrinsic interest is a key driver for sustained learning. Second, qualitative analysis revealed that learners perceived the alleviation of psychological burden and the provision of diagnostic and specific feedback as major advantages. Conversely, they identified technical limitations —such as vague, praise-oriented feedback, speech recognition errors—as well as the absence of non-verbal interaction as significant constraints. This study is significant for integrating AI into feedback and respeaking processes, and elucidating the psychological mechanisms of early users. The results underscore the instructor's mediating role in AI-integrated courses, and provide foundational data for the development of effective AI-assisted pedagogical models for general English education.
note: Gemini 역할극 말하기·피드백 학습자 인식 설문

title_ko: ChatGPT 기반 음성 상호작용에서 나타난 한국인 EFL 학습자의 영어 모음 /i/–/ɪ/ 발화에 대한 음향 분석
title_en: An acoustic analysis of Korean EFL learners’ production of the English vowel contrast /i/–/ɪ/ in ChatGPT-based interaction.
kw_en: ChatGPT; pronunciation; acoustic analysis; English vowels; feedback; Korean EFL learners
abstract_ko: The study explores whether interaction with ChatGPT’s speech-recognition feedback can improve Korean EFL learners’ production of the tense–lax vowel contrast /i/–/ɪ/. Korean university learners were divided into high- and low-proficiency groups and produced target words containing the two vowels up to five times during interaction with ChatGPT. Pronunciation changes were analyzed using recognition rate, acoustic measures (F1, F2), and Euclidean distance from native speaker vowel centroids. For the tense vowel /i/, both high- and low-proficiency groups showed significant F1 lowering, indicating a higher tongue position, while the low-proficiency group additionally exhibited F2 increase, reflecting greater tongue fronting toward the target vowel. For the lax vowel /ɪ/, however, acoustic changes were limited: F1 values showed minimal change, and clear convergence toward the native centroid was observed only in the high-proficiency group. These findings suggest that ChatGPT’s speech-recognition feedback can support articulatory adjustment and self-regulated pronunciation practice, particularly for L2 vowels close to learners’ L1 categories, whereas vowels without a direct L1 counterpart may require additional explicit instruction beyond ASR-based feedback .

title_ko: Tracing AI-Mediated Writing Tool Use Among Korean University Students: An Exploratory Screen-Recording Case Study
title_en: Tracing AI-Mediated Writing Tool Use Among Korean University Students: An Exploratory Screen-Recording Case Study
kw_en: AI-mediated writing; process-tracing; Korean EFL university students; English argumentative writing; critical AI literacy
abstract_ko: This exploratory case study uses process-tracing to examine how four Korean EFL university students utilize online dictionaries, machine translation, and ChatGPT during English argumentative writing. Analyzing screen recordings across three drafts, the study identifies specific tool-use purposes, sequences, and frequencies. Results reveal that tool-use trajectories are independent of English writing proficiency, reflecting idiosyncratic strategic choices and personal styles. Despite its potential, ChatGPT use remained minimal and surface-level due to study constraints, exposing a gap between AI’s potential and actual application. As the instructional design prioritized restricting AI, participants’ usage patterns demonstrated a tendency toward safe and basic routines, hindering the development of strategic digital writing skills. The study advocates for guided support to foster student agency and reflective practice. Ultimately, this process-oriented analysis provides a framework for curriculum designers seeking to integrate generative AI in ways that are both academically responsible and cognitively expansive.

title_ko: Reclaiming the Essay in the Age of AI: Teaching Writing as Thinking in the English Classroom
title_en: Reclaiming the Essay in the Age of AI: Teaching Writing as Thinking in the English Classroom
kw_en: writing as discovery; writing as experiment; Theodor Adorno; machine writing; writing pedagogy; artificial intelligence; college essay
abstract_ko: What does the essay accomplish in a GenAI-saturated world? We consider this problem through our experience of teaching college students as instructors of English literature. Rather than abandoning the form or defending it on nostalgic grounds, this article argues against the “death of the essay,” contending that the emergence of GenAI clarifies what is distinctive about human writing: a process by which a writer discovers and experiments with one’s thinking, and through which one is transformed. While LLMs can produce syntactically smooth prose and simulated coherence, these linguistic outcomes do not ensure the formation of a writerly subject. Recalling Donald Murray’s account of composition as process and David Russell’s critique of writing’s reduction to transferable skill, we turn to Theodor W. Adorno’s “The Essay as Form,” which defines essayistic writing as “writing while experimenting” and reframes essay writing as a reflective, relational epistemology. On these grounds, we propose a writing pedagogy that treats the essay as an experimental site of inquiry, not a polished end product. We illustrate this goal through two classroom activities: first, we discuss the “Writing as Discovery: Problem-Question-Motive” method that invokes students’ curiosity and converts interpretive puzzles into clear stakes and motives. We then discuss “Writing as Experiment: Situated Reading Journal,” which uses low-stakes first-person entries to register the importance of affect, exchange, and revision in critical writing. These models recast essay instruction as cultivating students’ capacity to visibly trace, revise, and own the movement of their thinking against the tide of machine-generated text.

title_ko: Exploring Student-AI Interaction Patterns in ChatGPT-Assisted Essay Writing
title_en: Exploring Student-AI Interaction Patterns in ChatGPT-Assisted Essay Writing
kw_en: Generative AI; ChatGPT; Student–AI interaction; Essay Writing; AI literacy
abstract_ko: This exploratory study examined how undergraduate students interacted with ChatGPT during essay-writing tasks, with a primary focus on identifying recurring student-AI interaction patterns. Participants were 21 undergraduates enrolled in an eight-week writing course at a private university in South Korea, where ChatGPT use was optional. Interaction transcripts from the 11 students who chose to use ChatGPT served as the primary data source, supplemented by surveys and interviews to contextualize how these patterns were experienced during writing. The analysis identified four recurring interaction patternsRepeatedStructure (RS), Creating Structure (CS), Modifying–Creating Structure (MCS), and Creating–Repeating Structure (CRS)-capturing how students repeated, generated, refined, and iteratively applied prompts while developing their essays. Students primarily used ChatGPT to develop body paragraphs, write conclusions, and revise drafts. They reported benefits such as improved idea organization and refined wording, while also noting redundancy, inaccuracies, and risks of overreliance. Survey and interview data further contextualized these patterns, highlighting students’ perceptions of ChatGPT as a tool for idea expansion, wording refinement, and revision. These findings underscore the dual role of generative AI in writing education and highlight the importance of guided and balanced integration to foster higherorderthinking and writing development.

title_ko: AI 디지털 기반 교수학습환경에서의 초등 영어과 맞춤형 수업 설계 모형 개발
title_en: Development of an adaptive instructional design model for elementary english education in AI-Enabled digital learning environments
kw_ko: AI 디지털 기반 수업; 초등 영어교육; 맞춤형 수업; 수업 설계 모형; 설계원리; 설계·개발 연구
kw_en: elementary English education; adaptive instruction; instructional design model; design principles; design and development research
abstract_ko: 교육현장에 AI 기반 학습 플랫폼이 도입되고 있으나, 초등 영어과의 교과 특수성을 반영하면서 AI, 에듀테크, 전통적 자료를 유연하게 통합할 수 있는 수업 설계 모형은 부족한 실정이다. 이에 본 연구는 AI 디지털 기반 교수학습환경에서 초등 영어 맞춤형 수업을 설계하기 위한 수업 설계 모형과 설계원리를 개발하고자 하였다. 이를 위해 설계·개발 연구 방법론을 적용하여 선행문헌 분석과 초등 영어 교사를 대상으로 한 경험적 탐색을 통해 설계원리 및 모형 초안을 도출하였다. 이후 교수설계, 초등영어교육, 교육공학 분야 전문가를 대상으로 2차례의 내적 타당화를 실시하여 6개 구성요소와 13개 설계원리를 개발하였다. 외적 타당화는 서울시 소재 초등학교 3학년 학습자 36명을 대상으로 총 8차시 수업을 설계·적용하고, 사전·사후 검사, 설문, 면담을 통해 효과를 검증하였다. 연구 결과, AI 활용 강도와 자료 유형을 기준으로 교사가 수업 맥락에 따라 7가지 수업 유형을 선택적으로 구성할 수 있는 이중축 선택형 수업 설계 모형이 개발되었다. 외적 타당화 결과, 학습자의 영어 말하기 정확성과 유창성이 유의미하게 향상되었으며, 학습 흥미, 자신감, 디지털 도구 효과성 인식은 증가하고 학습 불안감은 감소한 것으로 나타났다. 또한 교수자는 AI 활용 강도와 자료 유형을 조합하여 차시별로 다양한 수업 유형을 설계할 수 있었으며, 이를 통해 모형의 현장 활용 가능성이 확인되었다. 본 연구는 초등 영어과의 의사소통 중심 교수법적 특성을 반영하면서 교사가 수업 맥락에 따라 자료를 유연하게 조합할 수 있는 수업 설계 모형을 제시하였다는 점에서 의의가 있다. 다만 단일 학교 3학년을 대상으로 수행되어 연구 결과의 일반화에 한계가 있어, 다양한 학년과 교육 환경에서의 추가 검증이 요구된다.
abstract_en: Although AI-based learning platforms are being introduced in schools, there is still a lack of instructional design models that reflect the characteristics of elementary English and allow flexible use of AI, edutech, and traditional materials. This study aimed to develop instructional design principles and a model for adaptive elementary English instruction in an AI-enhanced digital learning environment. A design and development research approach was used, including a literature review, an exploratory study with elementary English teachers, and two rounds of expert validation. As a result, six components and thirteen design principles were developed. The model was applied in an eight-session class with 36 third-grade students. Data were collected through pre- and post-tests, surveys, and interviews. The results suggest that students’ speaking accuracy and fluency tended to improve, while interest, confidence, and perceived usefulness of digital tools increased, and anxiety decreased. Teachers were also able to design different lesson types based on the level of AI use and types of materials. These findings may suggest the potential use of the model in classroom settings. However, the study was conducted in one school, and further research in diverse contexts may be needed.
note: AI 디지털 환경 초등영어 맞춤형 수업설계 모형 개발·타당화

title_ko: AI 활용 영어 수업 및 평가에 대한 초등교사의 인식 및 정책 요구 분석: 중요도-수행도 분석을 중심으로
title_en: Elementary School English Teachers’ Perceptions and Policy Needs for AI-integrated Instruction and Assessment: Focusing on Importance-Performance Analysis
kw_ko: AI 활용 영어 교육; 초등영어교사; 중요도-수행도 분석(IPA); AI 기반 평가; 교육 정책
kw_en: AI-integrated English Education; Elementary English Teacher; Importance-Performance Analysis(IPA); AI-based Assessment; Educational Policy
abstract_ko: The purpose of this study is empirically to examine elementary English teachers’ perceptions and practical needs regarding AI-integrated instruction and assessment through a survey of 37 teachers using Importance-Performance Analysis(IPA). Results show that AI is widely used in instructional design, with over 90% adoption, mainly via the Google educational ecosystem. While instructional practices are stable, assessment areas-such as automated scoring, portfolios, and data-driven feedback-show significant gaps between importance and implementation. Key barriers include a lack of validated, subject-specific resources and limited professional development. The study recommends shifting AI policy from tool distribution to improving assessment reliability, developing subject-specific materials, and reinforcing teacher-in-the-loop systems to preserve pedagogical authority.
abstract_en: The purpose of this study is empirically to examine elementary English teachers’ perceptions and practical needs regarding AI-integrated instruction and assessment through a survey of 37 teachers using Importance-Performance Analysis(IPA).
